engineering.title: Stokes–Brinkman Porous Continuum, Helmholtz–Hodge Decomposition, and Percolation
engineering.subtitle: How viscous shear and Darcy drag balance over the Brinkman screening length √κ across porous limestone, capillary-active mortars, and consolidated geotechnical strata.

colophon.identifier: E.01 · Brinkman & Percolation · CSI 03 30 00 / 07 16 00
colophon.kernels: μ ∇²u − (μ/κ)u = ∇p · Discrete Helmholtz-Hodge
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: φ_c = 0.5927 (square-lattice site threshold) · √κ = 13.09 nm at defaults
colophon.bridge: Porous Stone & Mortar ↔ Capillary Pore Network Percolation

steps: Stage 1 (Supercritical Open Matrix, φ = 0.72): In the lattice model, connected pore channels span the domain; with a_f = 12 nm the Brinkman screening length is √κ = a_f φ^(3/2) / (2(1 − φ)) = 13.09 nm.

Stage 2 (Critical Percolation Backbone, φ → 0.5927): Tortuous dead-end branches multiply; transport restricts to a fractal spanning cluster. The value 0.5927 is the site-percolation threshold of the two-dimensional square lattice, used here as the model's threshold.

Stage 3 (Subcritical Arrest, φ < 0.5927): In the lattice model the open sites no longer connect across the domain, so its macroscopic conductivity is zero. Real three-dimensional pore networks stay connected at much lower porosity.
Stage 4 (Discrete Helmholtz-Hodge Decomposition): Separates velocity into curl-free pressure drive (−∇Φ) and divergence-free pore eddies (∇×Ψ).

skill.name: porous-brinkman-percolation
skill.description: AI-agnostic continuum and porous-media engineering skill for Darcy-Brinkman momentum screening, Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition, and continuum percolation (phi_c = 0.5927).
rules: Brinkman Screening Length: sqrt(kappa) = a_f * phi^(3/2) / (2 * (1 - phi)) from mu * nabla^2(u) - (mu/kappa)*u = nabla(p).

Lattice Percolation Threshold (model): compare porosity phi with phi_c = 0.5927, the site threshold of the 2D square lattice; the model scales effective diffusivity as ((phi - phi_c) / (1 - phi_c))^1.30. State that this is a lattice idealization; a real material needs its own measured threshold.
Discrete Helmholtz-Hodge Decomposition: Separate face-centered flux into L2-orthogonal curl-free potential gradient and divergence-free recirculation.

engineering.title: Herschel–Bulkley Yield-Stress Rheology: High-Performance Concrete Pumping & Tremie Placement
engineering.subtitle: How Eugene Bingham's and Winslow Herschel and Ronald Bulkley's yield-stress rheology describes pipe pressure drops, central plug-flow cores, and the risk of line blockage when concrete is pumped.
engineering.governing_law: τ = τ_0 + K γ̇^n · r_p / R = τ_0 / τ_w · ΔP/L = 2τ_w/R

colophon.identifier: E.02 · Concrete Yield Rheology · CSI 03 30 00
colophon.kernels: τ = τ_0 + K γ̇^n · Buckingham–Reiner Plug Flow
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: 125 mm pipe · τ_w = 75.0 Pa and r_p/R = 37.3% at defaults
colophon.bridge: Concrete Slickline

steps: Stage 1 (Unmobilized Solid Arrest, τ_w ≤ τ_0): When wall shear stress falls below yield stress τ_0, the concrete locks into zero-flow solid arrest.
Stage 2 (Central Unsheared Plug Core, r ≤ r_p): For τ_w > τ_0, an unsheared solid plug of radius r_p/R = τ_0/τ_w translates along the pipe center.

Stage 3 (Annular Shear-Thinning Layer): Shear is confined to the annulus r_p < r ≤ R. The page uses a power-law index n = 0.65 and consistency K = 8.5 Pa·sⁿ, fixed illustrative values rather than measured ones.
Stage 4 (Polycarboxylate Dispersion): PCE superplasticizers disperse cement grains and lower the yield stress; how much depends on the mix and dose, and the page does not model a specific reduction.

spec_plate.title: High-Performance Concrete Slickline Pumping & Tremie Placement
spec_plate.body: Illustrative design sketch, not a tested specification: a pumpable self-consolidating mix (target slump flow 650 mm, measured by the ASTM C1611 slump-flow test), a 125 mm steel line and a PCE superplasticizer, with the design rule that wall shear stress must exceed yield stress along the run.
spec_plate.meta: Design sketch · ACI 304.2R is the ACI guide to placing concrete by pumping; no field data or telemetry stand behind this plate

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.02-A · PLUG FLOW KINEMATICS & BUCKINGHAM–REINER
sidenote_1.body: In the ideal yield-stress model, concrete in the central core r ≤ r_p sees shear stress below τ_0, so it does not shear: the core moves as one piece at velocity u_plug. Real pumped concrete also forms a thin paste-rich layer at the wall, which this simple model leaves out.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.02-B · SPECIFICATION PLATE · CSI 03 30 00 / ACI 304.2R
sidenote_2.body: Design sketch of a pumped self-consolidating concrete (target slump flow 650 mm, 125 mm steel line, PCE dispersant).

skill.name: herschel-bulkley-yield-rheology
skill.description: AI-agnostic civil and non-Newtonian fluid mechanics skill for Herschel-Bulkley and Bingham concrete pumping rheology, plug-flow radius r_p/R = tau_0/tau_w, and thixotropic dispersion.
rules: Check slickline yield mobilization: pumping requires wall shear stress tau_w = (DeltaP * R)/(2L) > tau_0 (plug ratio r_p / R = tau_0 / tau_w < 1).
Evaluate Buckingham-Reiner volumetric flow multiplier Q / Q_Newtonian = 1 - (4/3)*(tau_0/tau_w) + (1/3)*(tau_0/tau_w)^4 for Bingham plastics.
Account for shear-thinning power-law index n < 1 in the sheared annulus, and state that real pumped concrete also forms a paste-rich lubrication layer at the wall that a homogeneous model leaves out.

engineering.title: Sub-Wavelength Acoustic Metamaterial Helmholtz Arrays and Viscothermal Boundary-Layer Damping
engineering.subtitle: How coiled-space resonators and viscothermal boundary layers δ_v = √(2ν/ω) can absorb low-frequency sound in panels far thinner than a quarter wavelength; the design study on this page targets about 1/19 of a wavelength.

colophon.identifier: E.03 · Acoustic Metamaterials & Viscothermal Damping · CSI 09 84 13
colophon.kernels: δ_v = √(2ν/ω) · Z_s = R_v + i ω M_a − i ρ c² / (ω V_cav)
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: δ_v = 0.174 mm at 160 Hz · α = 0.9996 for Z_s/Z_0 = 1.04 at resonance
colophon.bridge: Oscillatory Boundary Layers

steps: Stage 1 (Oscillatory Stokes Boundary Layer): At f_0 = 160 Hz, the viscous boundary layer in air is δ_v = √(2ν/ω) = 0.174 mm.
Stage 2 (Complex Effective Density & Bulk Modulus): When neck radius r_neck = 0.65 mm approaches 3.7 δ_v, viscous shear dissipates acoustic kinetic energy.

Stage 3 (Critical Impedance Matching, Z_s = Z_0): Reactance vanishes at Helmholtz resonance ω_0 while resistance matches ρ_0 c_0 ≈ 413 Pa·s/m. The page sets the resistance to 1.04 ρ_0 c_0 at the default neck radius, a fixed model value.

Stage 4 (Broadband Detuned Array): A design idea, not a built panel: several detuned coiled cavities could spread absorption over roughly 125–315 Hz in a panel about 110 mm deep (1/19 of the 2.14 m wavelength at 160 Hz).

skill.name: acoustic-helmholtz-metamaterial
skill.description: AI-agnostic acoustics and wave-mechanics engineering skill for sub-wavelength Helmholtz resonator arrays, Stinson viscothermal boundary-layer impedance, and critical coupling.
rules: Compute viscous boundary layer thickness delta_v = sqrt(2 * nu / omega) and Womersley number Wo = r_neck * sqrt(omega / nu) = sqrt(2) * r_neck / delta_v (so the ratio r_neck / delta_v equals Wo / sqrt(2)).
Enforce critical coupling condition Re(Z_surface) = rho_0 * c_0 and Im(Z_surface) = 0 at target resonance omega_0 for unity absorption.

Include an end-correction length in the effective neck inductance; the approximate form delta_l = 0.85 * r_neck * (1 - 1.25 * sqrt(porosity)) is this folio's working choice and should be checked against an acoustics reference before design use.

engineering.title: Counter-Current Enthalpy Recovery Exchangers: Effectiveness–NTU, Membrane Sorption, and Frost Limits
engineering.subtitle: Coupled sensible heat and latent water-vapor transfer across selective polymer membranes, with model values of 88.2% sensible and 79.4% latent effectiveness at the default settings and a simple frost-limit estimate.
engineering.governing_law: ε = NTU / (1 + NTU) · Bi_m = h_m δ_m / D_w · CSI 23 72 23

colophon.identifier: E.04 · Coupled Heat & Mass Transfer · CSI 23 72 23
colophon.kernels: ε = NTU / (1 + NTU) (Balanced Counter-Current)
colophon.bridge: Counter-Current Exchange ↔ How the Nose Warms and Humidifies Air (an analogy)

steps: Stage 1 (Balanced Counter-Current Flow, C_r = 1.0): At NTU = 7.5, sensible effectiveness reaches ε_s = NTU / (1 + NTU) = 7.5 / 8.5 = 88.2%.

Stage 2 (Membrane Vapor Permeation): Water vapor dissolves into and diffuses across a dense hydrophilic membrane. The page assumes a 25 μm membrane with Bi_m = 0.26, illustrative values; how well a real membrane holds back other gases depends on the product and was not modelled.

Stage 3 (Frost Threshold): Moving moisture across the membrane lowers the dew point of the exhaust stream, so frost starts at colder outdoor temperatures. The page uses a simple linear estimate, T_frost = −3.0 − 9.5 (ε_l / 79.4%) °C, which gives −12.5 °C at the defaults; it is an illustration, not a psychrometric calculation.

Stage 4 (Channel Geometry): Fully developed laminar flow between wide parallel plates has Nu ≈ 7.54 at constant wall temperature. The core pressure drop of 118 Pa at 2.1 m/s is a fixed illustrative value.

spec_plate.title: Counter-Current Polymer-Membrane Enthalpy Core & HEPA H14 Clean-Air Module
spec_plate.body: Illustrative design sketch, not a certified product: a counter-current enthalpy recovery core with a vapor-selective membrane and a separate HEPA filter stage. A low exhaust air transfer ratio (EATR) would be a design target to be measured; no value was measured for this page.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.04-A · AN ANALOGY: THE NOSE AS A HEAT AND MOISTURE EXCHANGER
sidenote_1.body: The nose warms and humidifies inhaled air and recovers some heat and water when we breathe out. That resembles an enthalpy exchanger, but it works by alternating flow over the same moist lining rather than by two streams on either side of a membrane. The comparison is an analogy offered by this folio.

skill.name: counter-current-enthalpy-exchanger
skill.description: AI-agnostic thermal and psychrometric engineering skill for counter-current heat and enthalpy recovery exchangers (epsilon-NTU), membrane moisture sorption, and frost-limit psychrometrics.
rules: For balanced counter-current flow (C_min / C_max = 1), compute effectiveness epsilon = NTU / (1 + NTU).
Evaluate membrane latent NTU_m = A_tot * U_m / m_dot_da where 1/U_m = 2/h_m + delta_m / D_eff_membrane.
Check exhaust plate surface temperature T_plate_cold > T_frost(omega_exhaust) to avoid ice blockage.

engineering.title: Terzaghi Soil Mechanics, CFA Augercast Deep Foundation Piling & Excess Pore Pressure
engineering.subtitle: How Karl Terzaghi's effective stress principle σ'_v = σ_v − u, hydrodynamic consolidation ∂u/∂t = c_v ∂²u/∂z², and Continuous Flight Auger (CFA) deep foundations relate to structural settlement and excess pore pressure.
engineering.governing_law: ∂u/∂t = c_v ∂²u/∂z² · Q_ult = Q_skin + Q_toe · r_u = Δu / σ'_{v0}

colophon.identifier: E.05 · Geotechnical & Deep Foundations · CSI 31 63 23
colophon.kernels: σ'_v = σ_v − u · ∂u/∂t = c_v ∂²u/∂z² · CFA Bearing
colophon.benchmarks: Model values at defaults: T_v = 0.320 · U_avg = 63.2% (H_dr = 6 m, t = 3.6 yr)
colophon.bridge: Terzaghi Consolidation

steps: Stage 1 (Undrained Surcharge Application, t = 0⁺): Structural surcharge Δq = 120 kPa transfers initially 100% into excess pore-water pressure Δu(z, 0) = Δq.

Stage 2 (Terzaghi Hydrodynamic Dissipation): Pore water drains toward permeable sand boundaries via ∂u/∂t = c_v ∂²u/∂z². The page assumes a drainage path H_dr = 6 m and an elapsed time t = 3.6 years, so T_v = 3.2 × 3.6 / 6² = 0.320 and U_avg = 1 − (8/π²) exp(−π² T_v / 4) = 63.2%.

Stage 3 (CFA Augercast Shaft + Toe Mobilization): A 750 mm diameter, 24 m deep CFA pile carries load by shaft friction and toe bearing. The page uses fixed illustrative capacities of 2,380 kN (shaft) and 1,980 kN (toe), and the folio assumes that residual pore pressure reduces them by factors of 0.65 r_u (shaft) and 0.35 r_u (toe): Q_ult = 2,380 × (1 − 0.65 r_u) + 1,980 × (1 − 0.35 r_u). With r_u = 0.221 (Stage 4, unrounded) this gives Q_ult = 3,865 kN against an assumed design load of 1,400 kN + 1.25 kN per kPa of surcharge (FS = 2.49). The 0.65 and 0.35 factors are this folio's own assumptions, not code values.

Stage 4 (Pore-Pressure Ratio, r_u = Δu / σ'_{v0}): The residual excess pore pressure after consolidation, Δu = Δq (1 − U_avg) = 44.2 kPa, over an assumed σ'_{v0} = 200 kPa gives r_u = 0.22. This is a consolidation ratio, not a seismic liquefaction analysis; r_u = 1 would mean zero effective stress, and the page flags r_u ≥ 0.70 as its own screening choice.

spec_plate.body: Illustrative design sketch, not a project specification: CFA piles (D = 750 mm, L = 24 m, f'_c = 40 MPa grout) installed with automated monitoring of depth, torque and pumped grout volume. The grout-volume target of more than 115% of theoretical volume is a design assumption of this page; check the current FHWA guidance for the actual criteria.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.05-A · TERZAGHI EFFECTIVE STRESS & TIME FACTOR T_v
sidenote_1.body: Consolidation settlement depends on the dimensionless time factor T_v = c_v t / H_dr². A clay layer drained at top and bottom (H_dr = H/2) reaches a given degree of consolidation 4× faster than the same layer drained on one side only.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.05-B · SPECIFICATION PLATE · CSI 31 63 23 (CFA PILES)

skill.name: terzaghi-cfa-geotechnical-piling
skill.description: AI-agnostic civil geotechnical engineering skill for Terzaghi 1D consolidation (du/dt = c_v d^2u/dz^2), effective stress sigma'_v = sigma_v - u, CFA deep foundation capacity, and excess pore-pressure r_u screening.
rules: Compute Terzaghi dimensionless time factor T_v = (c_v * t) / H_dr^2 and degree of consolidation U_avg = sqrt(4*T_v/pi) for T_v <= 0.286 or U_avg = 1 - (8/pi^2)*exp(-pi^2 * T_v / 4) for T_v > 0.286.

Evaluate axial CFA pile ultimate capacity Q_ult = Q_skin + Q_toe using effective overburden stress sigma'_v(z) = sigma_v(z) - u(z); this folio assumes the shaft term is scaled by (1 - 0.65 r_u) and the toe term by (1 - 0.35 r_u), its own illustrative factors.

Flag the design for review whenever excess pore-pressure ratio r_u = Delta_u / sigma'_v0 >= 0.70 or factor of safety FS = Q_ult / P_design < 2.0 (both are this folio's screening choices, not code values); a real liquefaction assessment needs a site-specific cyclic analysis.

steps: Stage 1 (Fixed-Base Response): The page assumes S_D1 = 0.60 S_DS, so at S_DS = 1.00 g the spectral plateau ends at T_s = 0.60 s. An unisolated frame with T_fixed = 0.65 s sits just past it, at S_a = 0.60/0.65 = 0.92 g.

Stage 2 (Lead-Rubber Period Lengthening, T_M = 2.85 s): Lengthening the period to 2.85 s moves the building onto the 1/T branch, S_a = 0.60/2.85 = 0.21 g, about 77% below the fixed-base value before any damping is counted.

Stage 3 (Bilinear Lead-Core Hysteretic Energy Dissipation): Plastic shear yielding of the central lead plug dissipates E_loop = 4 Q_d (D_M − D_y) per cycle. The page takes β_eff = 22% from the slider rather than computing it from the bearing properties, and B_M = 1.54 by interpolating 1.5 (20%) and 1.7 (30%).

Stage 4 (Model Check, Not a Code Check): With D_M = g S_D1 T_M / (4π² B_M) the model gives D_M = 276 mm, inside the assumed 400 mm moat, and C_s = S_D1 / (T_M B_M) = 0.137. Drift, floor acceleration and a full ASCE/SEI 7-22 Chapter 17 design were not checked.

skill.description: AI-agnostic structural dynamics and earthquake engineering skill for ASCE 7-22 Chapter 17 seismic base isolation, bilinear lead-rubber bearing hysteresis, and inelastic response spectra.
rules: Compute secant isolator stiffness k_eff = Q_d / D_M + k_d and effective isolated period T_M = 2 * pi * sqrt(W / (g * k_eff)).
Evaluate bilinear hysteretic loop energy E_loop = 4 * Q_d * (D_M - D_y), equivalent viscous damping beta_eff = E_loop / (2 * pi * k_eff * D_M^2), and ASCE 7-22 damping factor B_M.

Check that the design displacement D_M = (g * S * T_M) / (4 * pi^2 * B_M) stays within the moat clearance and that story drift meets the limits of the governing code; take the spectral value S, the B_M table and the drift limits from the current edition of the standard, not from this skill.

steps: Stage 1 (Modal Kinematics): Model 2,100 m span (B = 36 m) with heave h(x,t) (f_h = 0.095 Hz) and torsion α(x,t) (f_α = 0.235 Hz); illustrative values, not a surveyed bridge.

spec_plate.body: Design study: vented twin-box steel girder with a 6.0 m central slot, fairings, and an 8-station accelerometer and fiber-Bragg-grating array paired with a proposed PINN monitor.
spec_plate.meta: Design study · U_crit = 76.4 m/s is a model value, not a wind-tunnel result · no code compliance is claimed

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.07-A · WHY TACOMA NARROWS WAS FLUTTER, NOT SIMPLE VORTEX RESONANCE
sidenote_1.body: Vortex shedding occurs near f_s = St · U / D (about 1 Hz at 19 m/s), whereas Tacoma Narrows twisted near 0.2 Hz. Billah & Scanlan (1991, DOI 10.1119/1.16590) attribute the collapse to self-excited torsional flutter (A_2*(K) > 0).

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.07-B · SPECIFICATION PLATE · CSI 05 12 00 / PINN VIRTUAL SENSING
sidenote_2.body: Penalizing bending E I ∂⁴h/∂x⁴ − H_w ∂²h/∂x² + m ∂²h/∂t² − L_aero(x,t) and torsion I_α ∂²α/∂t² − G J ∂²α/∂x² − M_ae(x,t) might curb unphysical curvature spikes between sparse sensors if wind loads are estimated.

skill.name: bridge-flutter-pinn-twin
skill.description: AI-agnostic structural and wind civil engineering skill for Scanlan bridge aeroelastic flutter derivatives, critical wind speed U_crit, and Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) virtual stress sensing.
rules: Compute U_red = U / (f_alpha * B) and K = B * omega / U = 2 * pi / U_red.

Under Scanlan 1971 2B^2 moment scaling (per-span I_alpha in kg*m^2/m), evaluate zeta_net = zeta_s - (rho * B^4 / (2 * I_alpha)) * A_2*^(1971)(K) = zeta_s - (rho * B^4 / (4 * I_alpha)) * A_2*^(1996)(K) with A_2*^(1996) = 2 * A_2*^(1971); flutter starts at zeta_net <= 0.

Weight non-dimensionalized bending (E I ∂⁴h/∂x⁴ − H_w ∂²h/∂x² + m ∂²h/∂t² − L_aero) and torsion (I_α ∂²α/∂t² − G J ∂²α/∂x² − M_ae) residuals in L_total = L_data + λ_pde ‖R_pde‖²; unmeasured wind makes sparse inversion ill-posed.
State that these are explanatory single-mode relations with illustrative constants: not a design or assessment method, and no value here applies to a real bridge.

colophon.kernels: Lucas–Washburn Imbibition · Michaelis–Menten CaCO₃ · Coda-Wave CWI
colophon.benchmarks: Model: w_0 = 0.30 mm → w_rem = 0.018 mm (94.0% closure, illustrative) ⇒ (0.018/0.30)³ = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ ⇒ −99.98% parallel-plate flow (w³ law)
colophon.bridge: Continues E.01/E.07

steps: Stage 1 (Lucas–Washburn Capillary Imbibition): A flexural microcrack of width w_0 = 0.30 mm, treated as a parallel-plate channel (r = w_0/2), draws moisture to depth z(t) = √(γ w_0 cos θ · t / 4μ), wetting embedded bacterial spores.

Stage 2 (Spore Germination & Lactate-to-Calcite Conversion): Alkali-resistant bacteria metabolize calcium lactate, and calcium carbonate precipitates along the crack walls (the mechanism tested by Jonkers et al. 2010).

Stage 3 (Cubic Parallel-Plate Flow, Q ∝ w³): In this model, narrowing w from 0.30 mm to an illustrative 0.018 mm (94.0% closure) gives (0.018/0.30)³ = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴, a 99.98% cut in idealized laminar flow. Real healed cracks are rough and partly filled, so this is an upper-bound idealization.

Stage 4 (Ultrasonic Coda-Wave Interferometry): Multiply scattered ultrasonic coda waves are sensitive to very small relative velocity changes Δv/v, so CWI could be used to track stiffness recovery; the 96.4% recovery index shown in the lab is an illustrative model value, not a measurement.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.09-A · CONTINUING FOLIO E.01 CAPILLARY & CUBIC POISEUILLE SCALING
sidenote_1.body: For laminar flow between smooth parallel plates, discharge scales as Q ∝ w³ (Witherspoon et al. 1980, DOI 10.1029/WR016i006p01016). Cutting crack width by 90% would lower ideal flow 1,000-fold (0.1³ = 10⁻³), though real rough fracture walls depart from smooth plates.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.09-B · CODA-WAVE INTERFEROMETRY
sidenote_2.body: Coda-Wave Interferometry (CWI) uses late-arriving, multiply scattered waves to resolve tiny velocity changes Δv/v (Snieder 2006, DOI 10.1007/s00024-005-0026-6; Larose & Hall 2009, DOI 10.1121/1.3079771). Here it is proposed, not tested, for bridge-deck healing (continuing Folio E.07).

steps: Stage 1 (Nozzle Shear Rejuvenation, Continuing E.02): High shear inside the robotic printhead breaks colloidal links; this folio takes an illustrative initial yield stress τ_{0,0} = 420 Pa at deposition.

Stage 2 (Roussel Linear Thixotropic Structuration): At rest, flocculation and early hydration rebuild static yield stress, modelled as τ_0(t) = τ_{0,0} + A_thix t (A_thix = 0.85 Pa/s). The linear law is a short-time approximation; over longer times strength can grow faster than linearly.

Stage 3 (Plastic Yield vs. Suiker Buckling): The bottom layer must resist gravity shear τ_b = ρ g H / √3 (the von Mises criterion). With ρ = 2,200 kg/m³ (assumed) and v_build = 1.6 m/hr, gravity shear grows at 5.5 Pa/s against A_thix = 0.85 Pa/s, so in this model the base yields at H ≈ 0.04 m. Self-weight elastic buckling (Suiker 2018) also limits wall height; it is not computed on this page.

Stage 4 (Corrugated Funicular Toolpath, Continuing A.01): Corrugating the toolpath raises the wall's second moment of area and so its buckling resistance; this folio does not compute by how much, or how much cement it saves.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.10-A · CONTINUING FOLIO E.02 FROM PIPE FLOW TO FREE STANDING WALL
sidenote_1.body: While Folio E.02 minimized τ_0 to reduce slickline pumping pressure, a printed wall needs the opposite at rest. In the linear model, steady printing needs A_thix > ρ g v_build / √3: about 5.5 Pa/s at 1.6 m/hr for ρ = 2,200 kg/m³, or a maximum rate of about 0.25 m/hr at A_thix = 0.85 Pa/s.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.10-B · COLD-JOINT GUARD (DESIGN ASSUMPTION)
sidenote_2.body: Layer cycle time t_cycle should stay below the time the surface stays workable, here an assumed t_open = 18 min, to limit weak cold joints between layers. The 18 min figure is illustrative, not from a standard.

skill.name: 3dcp-roussel-thixotropy-buildability
skill.description: AI-agnostic additive civil engineering skill for 3D Concrete Printing (3DCP) Roussel thixotropic structuration (tau_0(t) = tau_00 + A_thix * t), plastic yield collapse, and Suiker elastic wall buckling.
rules: Evaluate static yield stress evolution tau_0(t) = tau_00 + A_thix * t and require A_thix > (rho * g * v_build) / sqrt(3) to prevent bottom-layer plastic collapse.
Remember that self-weight elastic buckling (Suiker 2018) also limits wall height; this folio does not compute it, so its H_crit is the plastic-collapse height H_plast only.
Verify interlayer cycle time t_cycle = L_perim / v_nozzle stays below open time t_open to prevent interfacial cold joints.

colophon.benchmarks: V/V_0 = 0.35 · p = 3.0 ⇒ 1 − V/V_0 = 65% less slab concrete volume · b/m = 0.18 inerter ratio (drift reduction not computed)
colophon.bridge: Continues E.10/A.01 · Trabecular Bone Remodeling (Wolff's Law) ↔ Robotic 3DCP Funicular Floor Ribs

steps: Stage 1 (Wolff's Trabecular Bone Remodeling & Principal Stress Trajectories): Under gravity and wind loads, a continuum finite-element model (FEniCS/dolfinx is one open-source tool a reader could use; this folio ran no FE model) gives principal tensile and compressive stress trajectories σ_1, σ_2.

Stage 2 (SIMP Power-Law Penalization & Helmholtz PDE Filtering): Element stiffness E_e(ρ_e) = E_min + ρ_e^p (E_0 − E_min) with p = 3 pushes intermediate densities toward 0 or 1, while a filter radius r_min suppresses checkerboard patterns and mesh dependency.

Stage 3 (Toward Michell-like Layouts): For simple load cases, optimized layouts tend to resemble Anthony Michell's 1904 minimum-weight trusses. Keeping V/V_0 = 0.35 means 65% less concrete volume in the optimized slab region than a solid slab of the same envelope; whole-building savings would be smaller.

Stage 4 (Flywheel Inerter): A ball-screw or rack-and-pinion flywheel inerter F = b(ü_2 − ü_1) has inertance b much larger than its own mass: for a ring flywheel on a screw, b = m_fly (2π r / P)², so r = 45 mm and lead P = 20 mm give b ≈ 200 m_fly (illustrative). Inerter-based devices have been studied for structural vibration suppression (Lazar et al. 2013); the drift reduction in the lab is illustrative.

spec_plate.body: Design study: formwork-free 3D-printed ribbed slabs shaped by Helmholtz-filtered SIMP topology optimization (p = 3, r_min = 45 mm assumed) paired with ball-screw flywheel inerters in tall-building outriggers. Not designed to or checked against any code.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.11-A · CROSS-FIELD ANALOGY · YOUR THIGH BONE & A FLYWHEEL
sidenote_1.body: Your femur is dense along the main load paths and lighter elsewhere, an observation behind Wolff's Law. Topology optimization removes material in a similar spirit. Lighter floors make tall buildings livelier in wind, which is where inerter-based dampers could help; the inerter is widely described as first used in Formula 1 suspensions (Lazar et al. 2013).

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.11-B · SENSITIVITIES & OPEN-SOURCE SOLVERS
sidenote_2.body: Adjoint sensitivities ∂c/∂ρ_e = −p ρ_e^(p−1)(E_0 − E_min) u_eᵀ k_0 u_e (as in Sigmund 2001) could be computed in open-source FEniCS/dolfinx. Neural surrogates such as physics-informed neural networks (Raissi et al. 2019) have been proposed to speed up such loops; this folio claims no speed-up.

skill.name: simp-topology-inerter-damping
skill.description: AI-agnostic structural engineering skill for Bendsøe-Sigmund SIMP continuum topology optimization, Helmholtz PDE sensitivity filtering, Michell funicular trusses, and tuned inerter dampers.
rules: Penalize intermediate element densities via SIMP law E_e(rho_e) = E_min + rho_e^p * (E_0 - E_min) with p >= 3 and E_min = 1e-9 * E_0.
Apply Helmholtz PDE density filter -r_min^2 * laplacian(rho_tilde) + rho_tilde = rho to enforce a mesh-independent minimum member size.
Size two-terminal flywheel inerter inertance b (kg) via F = b * (a_2 - a_1) to achieve target apparent-mass ratio mu_b = b / m_modal.

engineering.subtitle: Synthesizing Folio E.06's critical infrastructure protection, P.02's Kuramoto oscillators, and M.07's optimal control: how virtual synchronous machine inverters and Control Barrier Functions can steady a low-inertia renewable grid, and what a machine-checked RISC-V processor would add underneath.
engineering.governing_law: sup_u [L_f h(x) + L_g h(x) u] ≥ −α(h(x)) · M dΔω/dt + D Δω = P_m − P_e

colophon.identifier: E.12 · RISC-V & Grid Control Barrier Functions
colophon.kernels: Control Barrier Function h(x) ≥ 0 (Ames et al. 2017) · Swing Equation · Kami / Coq (Rocq) processor-proof precedents
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: RoCoF 0.42 Hz/s · h(x_grid) = +0.72 Hz · processor proof assumed, not shown
colophon.bridge: Synthesizes E.06/P.02/M.07 · Firefly Phase-Locking ↔ Grid-Forming Inverters

sliders.label: CBF Barrier Rate (α_CBF; higher = later intervention)

steps: Stage 1 (Firefly-Style Phase-Locking on the Power Grid, Continuing P.02): Solar and battery grid-forming inverters hold a common rhythm through coupled phase angles θ_i, M d²θ_i/dt² + D dθ_i/dt = P_i − ∑ K_ij sin(θ_i − θ_j), a member of the coupled-oscillator family studied in 'Synchronization in complex oscillator networks and smart grids' (Dörfler, Chertkov & Bullo 2013, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1212134110). The firefly is an analogy, not the same equation.

Stage 2 (Synthetic Inertia via Virtual Synchronous Machines): In the folio model, when a 1.2 GW loss hits, battery inverters inject power proportional to −H_virt dω/dt, in the manner of synchronverters (Zhong & Weiss 2011, DOI 10.1109/TIE.2010.2048839), and at the default H_virt = 4.8 s the initial Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) is 0.42 Hz/s. It stays below 0.5 Hz/s only for H_virt above about 4.0 s.

Stage 3 (Control Barrier Function Quadratic Program Filter, Continuing M.07): A real-time QP filter enforces L_f h(x) + L_g h(x)u ≥ −α(h(x)). For the modelled dynamics, and while the QP stays feasible, the state x does not leave the safe set h(x) ≥ 0 (Ames et al. 2017, DOI 10.1109/TAC.2016.2638961).

Stage 4 (Processor Layer, a Design Assumption): The filter is only as sound as the chip that runs it. Machine-checked RISC-V processors exist at small scale: Kami (Choi et al. 2017, DOI 10.1145/3110268) and the embedded system of Erbsen et al. (2021, DOI 10.1145/3453483.3454065), both in the Coq proof assistant, now named Rocq. This folio knows of no published machine-checked proof for the processor of a grid protection relay; here it is assumed, not shown.

spec_plate.title: Grid-Forming Virtual Synchronous Inverters with a Control Barrier Function Safety Filter
spec_plate.body: Distributed battery and solar grid-forming inverters governed by a Control Barrier Function (CBF-QP) safety filter. The filter is specified to run on a RISC-V processor whose formal proof is a design assumption of this folio, modelled on published Coq (Rocq) and Kami work.
spec_plate.meta: Anchors: Ames et al. 2017, DOI 10.1109/TAC.2016.2638961 · Dörfler, Chertkov & Bullo 2013, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1212134110

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.12-A · CROSS-FIELD ANALOGY · FIREFLIES FLASHING AS ONE
sidenote_1.body: Coal and hydro turbines steadied the 60 Hz grid with spinning steel. Solar panels have no moving parts, so grid-forming inverters are programmed to behave like a rotating machine and to fall into step with their neighbours, much as fireflies along a riverbank come to flash together. The network that such inverters would sit in can be described in the open-source toolbox PyPSA/PyPSA; the swing dynamics on this page are the folio's own reduced model.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.12-B · VERIFIED HARDWARE · HARDWARE CHECKED SO FAR
sidenote_2.body: Kami (Choi et al. 2017, DOI 10.1145/3110268) is a library for the Coq proof assistant, now named Rocq, for specifying and verifying hardware; its case study covers multicore systems with pipelined cores implementing the base integer subset of RISC-V. Erbsen et al. (2021, DOI 10.1145/3453483.3454065) report a simple embedded system whose application software, device drivers, compiler and RISC-V processor are one object in Coq with a machine-checked proof of functional correctness. Neither is a grid relay. A verified protection processor is the open step this folio argues for.

skill.name: verified-riscv-cbf-grid-sync
skill.description: AI-agnostic cyber-physical systems skill for Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) grid-forming inverters, Control Barrier Function (CBF-QP) forward invariance, and the published Coq (Rocq) and Kami precedents for machine-checked RISC-V processors.
rules: Enforce Nagumo forward invariance of safe set C = {x : h(x) >= 0} via CBF constraint L_f h(x) + L_g h(x) * u >= -alpha * h(x).
Bound grid Rate of Change of Frequency |df/dt| <= f_0 * Delta_P / (2 * H_virt * S_base); the folio model targets less than 0.5 Hz/s after the loss of one large unit.

Treat processor correctness as a stated assumption. Cite published machine-checked RISC-V work (Kami, DOI 10.1145/3110268; Erbsen et al. 2021, DOI 10.1145/3453483.3454065) and never claim a verified relay processor without a public proof artifact.

engineering.title: Biot 3D Poroelasticity, Skempton Undrained Coupling & Mohr–Coulomb Fault Slip Margin in Geologic CO2 Storage
engineering.subtitle: Continuing Folio E.01's porous percolation and E.05's 1D Terzaghi consolidation: an illustrative geomechanical study coupling Biot's 3D effective-stress coefficient α = 1 − K_d/K_s, Rice–Cleary Skempton pore-pressure response B, and cohesionless Mohr–Coulomb fault slip tendency τ/σ'_n across sedimentary storage basins and critically stressed crystalline basement.
engineering.governing_law: α = 1 − K_d / K_s · Δp_u = +B Δσ_mean · |τ| / (σ_n − α_fault(p_0 + Δp_inj)) < μ_f

colophon.identifier: E.13 · Biot Poroelasticity & Fault Slip Margin · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: Biot 3D Consolidation (1941) · Rice–Cleary Skempton B (1976) · Mohr–Coulomb Fault Slip Margin
colophon.benchmarks: Model values (sedimentary k_0 = 0.72, Δp_inj = 4.5 MPa): α = 0.667 · B = 0.394 (brine) / 0.053 (CO2) · τ/σ'_n = 0.404 < 0.60 · Δp_crit = 9.40 MPa
colophon.bridge: Continues E.01/E.05

steps: Stage 1 (Biot–Willis 3D Effective Stress, Continuing E.05): Whereas Terzaghi's 1D soil limit treats solid grains as incompressible (α → 1), stiff porous sandstone with drained bulk modulus K_d = 12.0 GPa and solid mineral grain modulus K_s = 36.0 GPa carries part of the hydrostatic stress in its grain skeleton, yielding α = 1 − K_d / K_s = 0.667 (Biot 1941, DOI 10.1063/1.1712886; Biot & Willis 1957, DOI 10.1115/1.4011606).

Stage 2 (Skempton Undrained Pore-Pressure Response B): Under compression-positive geomechanics (Δp_u = +B Δσ_mean), Skempton (1954, DOI 10.1680/geot.1954.4.4.143) and Rice & Cleary (1976, DOI 10.1029/RG014i002p00227) write B = (1/K_d − 1/K_s) / [1/K_d − 1/K_s + φ(1/K_f − 1/K_s)]. For φ = 0.20 and brine bulk modulus K_f = 2.2 GPa, B = 0.394; replacing brine with compressible supercritical CO2 (K_f = 0.20 GPa) lowers B to 0.053 in the folio model.

Stage 3 (Mohr–Coulomb Fault Slip Margin & Stress-Regime Contrast): On a cohesionless fault dipping 60° (fault-plane angle β = 30° from vertical σ_v, normal 30° from σ_h; σ_v = 50.0 MPa, hydrostatic p_0 = 20.0 MPa, μ_f = 0.60, α_fault = 1.0, and uncoupled total stress σ_h = k_0 σ_v), a sedimentary stress ratio k_0 = 0.72 gives σ_n = 39.50 MPa, τ = 6.062 MPa, and Δp_crit = 9.40 MPa; at Δp_inj = 4.5 MPa, slip tendency τ/σ'_n = 0.404 stays below 0.60. In a critically stressed crystalline basement (k_0 = 0.60), Δp_crit drops to 0.57 MPa and Δp_inj = 4.5 MPa raises τ/σ'_n to 0.825 (> 0.60).

Stage 4 (Open Hypothesis, Tier T1–T2, and Falsification Condition): Hypothesis (Tier T1–T2): in stiff porous sedimentary storage reservoirs where stress ratio k_0 keeps Δp_inj < Δp_crit and compressible supercritical CO2 lowers undrained B while keeping overpressure moderate (Vilarrasa & Carrera 2015, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1413284112), fault slip tendency remains below μ_f; this hypothesis is falsified in any site where pore pressure reaches critically stressed basement faults (Zoback & Gorelick 2012, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1202473109; Ellsworth 2013, DOI 10.1126/science.1225942), drives σ'_n ≤ 0, or where coupled poroelastic stress transfer pushes |τ|/σ'_n ≥ μ_f.

spec_plate.division: SUBSURFACE GEOMECHANICS / CSI 31 00 00 (FILING LABEL · DESIGN STUDY)
spec_plate.title: Deep Saline Aquifer CO2 Storage Reservoir & Caprock Pressure-Management Envelope
spec_plate.body: Illustrative geomechanical screening study, not a site-specific reservoir permit or injection design: tracks Biot matrix coupling (α = 0.667, passive lateral stress-path index η_poro = 0.444), cohesionless Mohr–Coulomb fault slip tendency (α_fault = 1.0, μ_f = 0.60, holding σ_h = k_0 σ_v uncoupled from Δp_inj), and minimum-principal-stress hydraulic fracture margin (min(σ_v, σ_h) − p_0 − Δp_inj = 11.50 MPa at defaults). Field characterization and coupled 3D multiphase flow-geomechanics modeling are required for any real injection project.
spec_plate.meta: Primary anchors: Biot 1941 (DOI 10.1063/1.1712886) · Rice & Cleary 1976 (DOI 10.1029/RG014i002p00227) · Zoback & Gorelick 2012 (DOI 10.1073/pnas.1202473109) · Vilarrasa & Carrera 2015 (DOI 10.1073/pnas.1413284112) · Model values, not field measurements

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.13-A · OPEN SCIENTIFIC DEBATE · SEDIMENTARY RESERVOIRS VS. BASEMENT FAULTS
sidenote_1.body: Zoback & Gorelick (2012, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1202473109) warned that large-scale geologic carbon dioxide injection into brittle continental-interior rocks carries a substantial probability of triggering small-to-moderate earthquakes that could threaten caprock seal integrity. Vilarrasa & Carrera (2015, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1413284112; reply DOI 10.1073/pnas.1511302112) countered that soft sedimentary basins are less critically stressed than crystalline basement, while brine displacement and dissolution limit overpressure. Ellsworth (2013, DOI 10.1126/science.1225942) documented how deep wastewater injection near basement faults drove midcontinent seismicity, showing why basal fault proximity governs operational risk.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.13-B · MATRIX α, FAULT α_fault & UNCOUPLED TOTAL-STRESS CAVEAT
sidenote_2.body: Intact porous sandstone shares load across mineral grain contacts (α = 1 − K_d/K_s = 0.667), giving a lateral poroelastic stress-path index η_poro = α(1 − 2ν)/(1 − ν) = 0.444 at ν = 0.25. Along a damaged or open fault surface, conservative Mohr–Coulomb screening uses α_fault = 1.0 consistently in both σ'_n = σ_n − α_fault(p_0 + Δp_inj) and Δp_crit. In this reduced closed-form model, η_poro is reported passively while total horizontal stress remains uncoupled at σ_h = k_0 σ_v rather than adding η_poro Δp_inj.

skill.name: biot-poroelasticity-fault-slip
skill.description: AI-agnostic civil geomechanics skill for Biot 3D poroelasticity (alpha = 1 - K_d/K_s), Rice-Cleary Skempton B coupling, and cohesionless Mohr-Coulomb fault slip margin under subsurface fluid injection.
rules: Compute intact-matrix Biot-Willis coefficient alpha = 1 - K_d / K_s (requiring 0 < K_d < K_s) and Skempton undrained coefficient B = (1/K_d - 1/K_s) / [1/K_d - 1/K_s + phi*(1/K_f - 1/K_s)] under compression-positive sign convention delta_p_u = +B * delta_sigma_mean.

Keep fault-plane Terzaghi effective stress alpha_fault = 1.0 distinct from matrix alpha, and apply alpha_fault consistently in both sigma_n_eff = sigma_n - alpha_fault*(p_0 + delta_p_inj) and critical_delta_p = (sigma_n - |tau|/mu_f)/alpha_fault - p_0; state explicitly when total stress sigma_h is held uncoupled from eta_poro * delta_p_inj.

Check both shear slip tendency |tau| / sigma_n_eff < mu_f and tensile hydraulic margin min(sigma_v, sigma_h) - (p_0 + delta_p_inj) > 0; treat sigma_n_eff <= 0 explicitly as tensile failure with undefined shear slip tendency.

Frame injection stability as a site-dependent Tier T1-T2 hypothesis bounded by stress ratio k_0 and basement fault proximity; never extrapolate closed-form screening outputs into site-specific permit claims.

engineering.title: Unsaturated Soil Suction Stress, van Genuchten–Mualem Water Retention & Rainfall-Induced Infinite-Slope Instability
engineering.subtitle: Continuing Folio E.05's saturated Terzaghi effective stress and E.13's poroelastic fault margin: an illustrative geotechnical screening study coupling van Genuchten–Mualem retention S_e(ψ) and K_r(S_e), Lu–Godt–Wu closed-form suction stress σ^s = −S_e ψ, and infinite-slope limit equilibrium FS across wetting hillslopes and dry sands.
engineering.governing_law: S_e = [1 + (α_vG ψ)^n]^(−m) · σ^s = −S_e ψ · FS = tan φ' / tan β + (c' − σ^s tan φ') / (γ z sin β cos β)

colophon.identifier: E.14 · Unsaturated Suction Stress & Slope Margin · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: van Genuchten SWCC (1980) · Mualem K_r (1976) · Lu–Godt–Wu Suction Stress (2010)
colophon.benchmarks: Model values (silty loam ψ = 24.0 kPa, β = 34.0°): S_e = 0.904 · K_r = 0.1662 · σ^s = −21.69 kPa · FS = 1.557 (collapses to 0.962 at ψ = 2.0 kPa)
colophon.bridge: Continues E.05/E.13

sliders.label: Matric Suction at Slip Plane (ψ = u_a − u_w)

steps: Stage 1 (van Genuchten–Mualem Water Retention, Continuing E.05): Above the water table (ψ = u_a − u_w ≥ 0 kPa), soil pores hold both air and capillary water. van Genuchten (1980, DOI 10.2136/sssaj1980.03615995004400050002x) parameterizes effective saturation as S_e(ψ) = [1 + (α_vG ψ)^n]^(−m) with m = 1 − 1/n (requiring n > 1), and Mualem (1976, DOI 10.1029/WR012i003p00513) gives K_r(S_e) = S_e^(1/2) [1 − (1 − S_e^(1/m))^m]^2. In silty loam (α_vG = 0.02 kPa^−1, n = 1.60, m = 0.375) at ψ = 24.0 kPa, S_e = 0.904 and K_r = 0.1662.

Stage 2 (Lu–Godt–Wu Suction Stress σ^s and Pore-Exponent Split): Lu, Godt & Wu (2010, DOI 10.1029/2009WR008646) unify Bishop effective stress σ' = (σ − u_a) − σ^s via closed-form suction stress σ^s(ψ) = −S_e(ψ) ψ ≤ 0 (compression-positive convention, so negative σ^s pulls grains together). For silty loam (1 < n ≤ 2), |σ^s| rises monotonically (−21.69 kPa at ψ = 24.0 kPa; −65.34 kPa at ψ = 120.0 kPa). For clean sand (n = 2.68 > 2, α_vG = 0.145 kPa^−1), |σ^s| peaks at ψ_peak = 7.964 kPa (−4.52 kPa) and declines to −2.08 kPa by ψ = 40.0 kPa.

Stage 3 (Infinite-Slope Wetting Collapse While Still Unsaturated): Following Lu & Godt (2008, DOI 10.1029/2008WR006976) with steady uniform suction at z = 2.0 m, γ = 19.0 kN/m^3, c' = 2.0 kPa, and φ' = 28.0°, a steep silty-loam slope at β = 34.0° (> φ') stands at FS = 1.557 when ψ = 24.0 kPa. Rain wetting to ψ = 2.0 kPa drops FS to 0.962 (< 1.0) even before pore-water pressure turns positive, and saturation (ψ = 0 kPa, K_r = 1.0) drops FS to 0.902.

Stage 4 (Open Hypothesis, Tier T1–T2, and Falsification Condition): Hypothesis (Tier T1–T2): in shallow unsaturated hillslopes steeper than their drained friction angle (β > φ'), storm-triggered collapse below FS = 1.0 tracks the loss of S_e ψ during wetting rather than waiting for positive u_w, whereas setting Bishop χ = 1.0 on dry clean sand (ψ = 40.0 kPa, γ = 18.0 kN/m^3, c' = 0, φ' = 32°, β = 36°) falsely inflates FS from 0.936 to 2.320. This 1D steady-suction hypothesis is falsified where 3D topographic flow convergence, macropore bypass (Iverson 2000, DOI 10.1029/2000WR900090), wetting-branch hysteresis, or root cohesion governs field failure.

spec_plate.division: VADOSE GEOTECHNICS / CSI 31 32 00 (FILING LABEL · DESIGN STUDY)
spec_plate.title: Unsaturated Silty-Loam & Clean-Sand Hillslope Suction-Stress Screening Envelope
spec_plate.body: Illustrative closed-form screening study, not a site geotechnical investigation or slope-stability design: prescribes steady uniform matric suction ψ ≥ 0 kPa at slip-plane depth z = 2.0 m with constant unit weight γ = 19.0 kN/m^3 (silty loam) or 18.0 kN/m^3 (clean sand), α_vG expressed in kPa^−1 (1 kPa ≈ 10.194 cm H2O), and atmospheric pore-air pressure u_a = 0. Below the water table (u_w > u_a, ψ < 0), behavior transitions to saturated Terzaghi effective stress. Transient Richards infiltration, wetting-drying hysteresis, and field tensiometry are required for any real slope assessment.
spec_plate.meta: Primary anchors: van Genuchten 1980 (DOI 10.2136/sssaj1980.03615995004400050002x) · Mualem 1976 (DOI 10.1029/WR012i003p00513) · Lu, Godt & Wu 2010 (DOI 10.1029/2009WR008646) · Iverson 2000 (DOI 10.1029/2000WR900090) · Model values, not field measurements

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.14-A · FINE SILTY LOAM (n ≤ 2) VS. CLEAN SAND (n > 2) SUCTION PEAK
sidenote_1.body: Differentiating |σ^s(ψ)| = ψ [1 + (α_vG ψ)^n]^(−(n−1)/n) shows that d|σ^s|/dψ flips sign only when n > 2. In fine silty loam (n = 1.60 ≤ 2), adsorptive films and broad pore-size distributions sustain a monotonically growing tensile suction stress across the modeled suction range. In uniform clean sand (n = 2.68 > 2, α_vG = 0.145 kPa^−1), pendular capillary bridges break down past ψ_peak = 7.964 kPa (|σ^s| = 4.52 kPa), reducing |σ^s| to 2.08 kPa at ψ = 40.0 kPa and leaving dry sand at FS = 0.936 when β = 36° > φ' = 32°.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.14-B · STEADY PRESCRIBED ψ, CONSTANT γ & α_vG UNIT CONVENTION
sidenote_2.body: This reduced 2-slider model prescribes steady uniform ψ at z = 2.0 m and constant γ rather than integrating coupled transient Richards diffusion (Iverson 2000, DOI 10.1029/2000WR900090) or moisture-dependent unit weight γ(θ) (Lu & Godt 2008, DOI 10.1029/2008WR006976). Also check parameter units carefully: α_vG here uses kPa^−1 (matching ψ in kPa), whereas Carsel & Parrish soil tables report α in cm^−1 of water head (1 kPa ≈ 10.194 cm H2O). Below the water table (ψ < 0), saturated Terzaghi pore pressure applies.

skill.name: unsaturated-suction-slope
skill.description: AI-agnostic civil geotechnical skill for van Genuchten-Mualem unsaturated soil water retention, Lu-Godt-Wu closed-form suction stress sigma_s = -S_e * psi, and rainfall-induced infinite-slope Factor of Safety.
rules: Enforce the physical domain psi = u_a - u_w >= 0 kPa, alpha_vg > 0 kPa^-1, and n > 1.0 (m = 1 - 1/n in (0, 1)) for van Genuchten effective saturation S_e(psi) = [1 + (alpha_vg * psi)^n]^(-m) and Mualem relative hydraulic conductivity K_r(S_e).

Compute Lu-Godt-Wu closed-form suction stress as sigma_s(psi) = -S_e(psi) * psi <= 0 (with sigma_s = 0 at psi = 0), keeping effective weighting chi = S_e rather than extrapolating Terzaghi chi = 1.0 into unsaturated soil.

Distinguish fine-grained monotonic retention (1 < n <= 2, silty loam where |sigma_s| grows monotonically with suction) from coarse-grained non-monotonic retention (n > 2, clean sand where |sigma_s| peaks near air-entry and declines toward zero upon drying).

Frame infinite-slope stability as a steady-suction, constant-gamma Tier T1-T2 screening hypothesis that requires 3D seepage, wetting-drying hysteresis, and field tensiometry before any site-level slope evaluation.

engineering.title: Quasi-Brittle Concrete Fracture, Bažant Size Effect Law & Hillerborg Process-Zone Scaling
engineering.subtitle: Continuing Folio E.02's concrete placement, E.09's crack healing, and E.11's continuum stiffness: an illustrative fracture-mechanics study coupling Hillerborg's fictitious crack model, Bažant's Type II Size Effect Law, and Bažant–Kazemi regression for initial fracture energy and process-zone length across laboratory beams and deep concrete girders.

colophon.identifier: E.15 · Bažant Size Effect & Concrete Fracture · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: Griffith LEFM (1921) · Hillerborg Fictitious Crack (1976) · Bažant Size Effect Law (1984, 1990)
colophon.benchmarks: Model values (notched beam D = 400.0 mm, D_0 = 220.0 mm): β_B = 1.818 · σ_N = 2.502 MPa (59.6% of B f'_t) · s = −0.323 · G_f = 127.84 N/m · c_f = 64.84 mm (drops to σ_N = 1.322 MPa at D = 2000 mm)
colophon.bridge: Continues E.02/E.09/E.11

steps: Stage 1 (From Griffith LEFM to Hillerborg's Fictitious Crack Zone): Griffith (1921, DOI 10.1098/rsta.1921.0006) showed that a sharp crack in a brittle solid grows when stored elastic energy release matches surface energy, scaling nominal strength as D^(−1/2). Concrete is not ideally brittle: ahead of a visible notch, microcracking and aggregate bridging form a finite Fracture Process Zone (FPZ). Hillerborg, Modéer, and Petersson (1976, DOI 10.1016/0008-8846(76)90007-7) modeled this softening zone via tensile strength f'_t, initial fracture energy G_f, and characteristic length l_ch = E' G_f / (f'_t)^2 (424.5 mm at E' = 34.0 GPa, f'_t = 3.20 MPa, G_f = 127.84 N/m).

Stage 2 (Bažant Type II Size Effect Law & Brittleness Number β_B): For geometrically similar notched members (notch ratio α_0 = a_0 / D > 0), Bažant (1984, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9399(1984)110:4(518)) matched plastic yield at small D against LEFM at large D via σ_N(D) = B f'_t / √(1 + β_B), with brittleness number β_B = D / D_0. Using illustrative calibration B f'_t = 4.20 MPa and D_0 = 220.0 mm, a 100 mm laboratory beam reaches σ_N = 3.482 MPa (82.9% of B f'_t, β_B = 0.455), while a 400 mm beam drops to 2.502 MPa (59.6%, β_B = 1.818) and log–log slope s = −β_B / [2(1 + β_B)] steepens from −0.156 to −0.323.

Stage 3 (Bažant–Kazemi Regression for G_f and Process-Zone Length c_f): Bažant and Kazemi (1990, DOI 10.1007/BF00047063) inverted the size-effect curve into a linear relation Y = 1 / σ_N^2 = C D + A, where G_f = (B f'_t)^2 D_0 g(α_0) / E' and effective FPZ length c_f = D_0 g(α_0) / g'(α_0). With LEFM geometry factors g(α_0) = 1.12 and g'(α_0) = 3.80 at D_0 = 220.0 mm, the model yields G_f = 127.84 N/m and c_f = 64.84 mm. Doubling D_0 to 440.0 mm (a tougher aggregate mix at fixed B f'_t) raises G_f to 255.68 N/m, c_f to 129.68 mm, and 400 mm beam nominal strength to 3.040 MPa.

Stage 4 (Open Hypothesis, Tier T1–T2, and Falsification Condition): Hypothesis (Tier T1–T2): in geometrically similar notched concrete beams without distributed shear reinforcement, nominal failure stress declines along σ_N = B f'_t (1 + D / D_0)^(−1/2) toward Griffith D^(−1/2) scaling as structural depth grows; at D = 2000 mm (D_0 = 220 mm, β_B = 9.091), modeled σ_N falls to 1.322 MPa (31.5%, slope −0.450), whereas ignoring (1 + D / D_0) overpredicts capacity by 3.177× at 4.20 MPa. This Type II hypothesis is falsified in unnotched Type I beams governed by Weibull boundary-layer strength (Bažant & Yu 2009, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9399(2009)135:2(78)), in heavily stirrup-confined or steel-fiber members that arrest localization, or where aggregate size d_a is comparable to D.

spec_plate.division: CONCRETE FRACTURE / CSI 03 30 00 (FILING LABEL · DESIGN STUDY)
spec_plate.title: Bažant Type II Notched Concrete Fracture & Brittleness Scaling Screening Envelope
spec_plate.body: Illustrative closed-form fracture-scaling study, not a structural code check (ACI 318 / fib Model Code) or member design: tracks Type II geometrically similar notched specimens (notch ratio α_0 > 0, LEFM shape factors g(α_0) = 1.12 and g'(α_0) = 3.80, E' = 34.0 GPa, B f'_t = 4.20 MPa, f'_t = 3.20 MPa). Holding B f'_t, E', g(α_0), and g'(α_0) constant while sweeping transitional size D_0 scales initial fracture energy G_f, process-zone length c_f, and Hillerborg l_ch linearly with D_0, comparing tougher versus more brittle mixes at constant small-scale plastic strength. Unnotched Type I members, stirrup reinforcement, and full-scale testing fall outside this reduced 2-slider curve.
spec_plate.meta: Primary anchors: Griffith 1921 (DOI 10.1098/rsta.1921.0006) · Hillerborg et al. 1976 (DOI 10.1016/0008-8846(76)90007-7) · Bažant 1984 (DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9399(1984)110:4(518)) · Bažant & Kazemi 1990 (DOI 10.1007/BF00047063) · Model values, not laboratory test data

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.15-A · INITIAL FRACTURE ENERGY G_f VS. TOTAL WORK OF FRACTURE G_F
sidenote_1.body: Bažant and Kazemi (1990, DOI 10.1007/BF00047063) distinguish the initial fracture energy G_f—governed by the steep initial tangent of the cohesive softening curve and extracted from size-effect peak loads—from the larger total work of fracture G_F integrated under the entire softening tail. Peak-load structural size effect depends primarily on G_f and effective process-zone length c_f, whereas post-peak tail energy G_F governs late crack opening.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.15-B · TYPE II NOTCHED BOUNDARIES & CONSTANT-B f'_t PARAMETERIZATION
sidenote_2.body: This reduced 2-slider sweep holds B f'_t = 4.20 MPa, E' = 34.0 GPa, f'_t = 3.20 MPa, g(α_0) = 1.12, and g'(α_0) = 3.80 constant across D_0 ∈ [80, 500] mm, so G_f = (B f'_t)^2 D_0 g(α_0) / E', c_f, and l_ch all scale linearly with D_0 (comparing tougher versus more brittle mixes). The curve applies to notched Type II members (α_0 > 0); unnotched Type I beams retain a finite large-size asymptotic stress under Universal Size Effect Law (Bažant & Yu 2009, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9399(2009)135:2(78)).

skill.name: bazant-size-effect
skill.description: AI-agnostic civil structural fracture skill for Bazant Type II Size Effect Law, Hillerborg fictitious crack length l_ch, and Bazant-Kazemi extraction of fracture energy G_f and process-zone length c_f.
rules: Enforce strictly positive finite parameters D, D_0, B*f_t, E', f_t, g(alpha_0), and g'(alpha_0) inside geometrically similar notched Type II members (alpha_0 = a_0 / D > 0).

Compute nominal strength via Bazant Type II Size Effect Law sigma_N = B*f_t / sqrt(1 + D/D_0) with brittleness number beta_B = D / D_0 and log-log slope s = -beta_B / (2*(1 + beta_B)), avoiding scale-invariant plastic extrapolation.

Check unit identity (MPa^2 * mm / GPa = N/m) when evaluating initial Mode I fracture energy G_f = (B*f_t)^2 * D_0 * g(alpha_0) / E', effective FPZ length c_f = D_0 * g(alpha_0) / g'(alpha_0), and Hillerborg characteristic length l_ch = E' * G_f / f_t^2 (mm).
Frame Type II size-effect scaling as a Tier T1-T2 structural screening hypothesis that stops at unnotched Type I beams, stirrup-confined or fiber-reinforced shear members, and code design checks.

engineering.lineage_mode: CONTINUATION · Continues E.05 Deep Piling, E.07 Bridge Dynamics & E.14 Rainfall Slope Mechanics
engineering.title: Bridge Pier Local Scour, Shields Sediment Threshold & Flood-Duration Time-Scale Lag
engineering.subtitle: Continuing Folio E.05's deep piling, E.07's bridge dynamics, and E.14's rainfall slope mechanics: an illustrative hydraulic-engineering study coupling Shields incipient sediment motion, Sheppard and Melville equilibrium horseshoe-vortex scour, Federal Highway Administration Froude envelopes, and Melville and Chiew flood-duration lag around circular river bridge piers.

colophon.identifier: E.16 · Bridge Pier Scour & Flood Time-Scale Lag · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: Shields Threshold (1936) · Melville Pier Scour (1997) · Melville–Chiew Time Scale (1999) · Sheppard–Melville (2014)
colophon.benchmarks: Model values (circular pier a* = 2.00 m, y_1 = 3.00 m, d_50 = 2.00 mm, V_1 / V_c = 0.85, t_d = 24.0 h): V_c = 0.860 m/s · y_s,SM,eq = 2.505 m · y_s,CSU,eq = 2.142 m · t_e = 42.09 days · K_t = 0.7254 · y_s(24 h) = 1.817 m (1.213 m at 2.0 h flash flood)
colophon.bridge: Continues E.05/E.07/E.14

steps: Stage 1 (Shields Incipient Motion & Logarithmic Critical Velocity V_c): Forensic analysis of 503 United States bridge failures from 1989 to 2000 by Wardhana and Hadipriono (2003, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0887-3828(2003)17:3(144)) attributed 266 failures (52.88%) to hydraulic flood, scour, and debris forces. Under Shields incipient-motion mechanics (documented by Buffington 1999, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9429(1999)125:4(376)) and Melville (1997, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9429(1997)123:2(125)), cohesionless quartz grains (specific gravity s = 2.65, d_50 = 2.00 mm, θ_c = 0.045) reach critical shear velocity u_*c = √(θ_c (s − 1) g d_50) = 0.03817 m/s and depth-averaged threshold velocity V_c = 5.75 u_*c log_10(5.53 y_1 / d_50) = 0.860 m/s at approach depth y_1 = 3.00 m.

Stage 2 (Sheppard–Melville Equilibrium Scour vs. Froude-Only HEC-18 CSU): Sheppard, Melville, and Demir (2014, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)HY.1943-7900.0000800) evaluated 23 pier-scour formulas across 569 laboratory and 928 field records (filtered to 441 laboratory and 791 field datasets), merging clear-water factors into y_s,SM = 2.5 a* f_1 f_2 f_3 with f_1 = tanh((y_1 / a*)^0.4), f_2 = max(0, 1 − 1.2 [ln(V_1 / V_c)]^2), and f_3 = (a* / d_50) / [0.4 (a* / d_50)^1.2 + 10.6 (a* / d_50)^(−0.13)]. For a* = 2.00 m (f_1 = 0.8262, f_3 = 0.6263), near-threshold flow V_1 / V_c = 0.45 gives y_s,SM,eq = 0.608 m versus Froude-based CSU y_s,CSU,eq = 1.629 m (2.682× higher because CSU omits V_c), whereas near the clear-water peak V_1 / V_c = 0.85 gives y_s,SM,eq = 2.505 m versus y_s,CSU,eq = 2.142 m.

Stage 3 (Melville & Chiew Equilibrium Time Scale t_e and Transient Factor K_t): Melville and Chiew (1999, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9429(1999)125:1(59)) showed that clear-water horseshoe-vortex scour approaches equilibrium over time scale t_e (days) = 30.89 (a* / V_1) (V_1 / V_c − 0.4) (y_1 / a*)^0.25 for y_1 / a* <= 6.0 (where empirical constant 30.89 = 2.669 × 10^6 / 86,400 days·s^(−1) converts dimensionless t* = V_1 t_e,sec / a* with a* in m and V_1 in m/s), with temporal fraction K_t(t_d) = exp(−0.03 |(V_c / V_1) ln((t_d / 24) / t_e)|^1.6) for t_d / 24 < t_e (clamped to 1.0 once t_d / 24 >= t_e). At V_1 / V_c = 0.85 (V_1 = 0.731 m/s), t_e = 42.09 days (1,010.1 h): a 2.0 h flash flood reaches K_t = 0.4841 (y_s = 1.213 m), and a 24.0 h storm reaches K_t = 0.7254 (y_s = 1.817 m). Applying a relation fitted to steady laboratory flows to a 2.00 m pier and to a flood duration is an extrapolation.

Stage 4 (Open Hypothesis, Tier T1–T2, and Falsification Conditions): Hypothesis (Tier T1–T2): in uniform cohesionless sand or fine gravel around an unskewed circular pier under single-peak clear-water flow (0.45 <= V_1 / V_c <= 1.00), transient scour depth follows y_s(t_d) = K_t(t_d) y_s,SM,eq, excavating roughly half of equilibrium depth within two hours yet remaining below steady-state equilibrium across 24-hour floods (1.817 m vs. 2.505 m S/M and 2.142 m CSU). This hypothesis is falsified under live-bed sediment transport (V_1 / V_c > 1.0), in graded armored riverbeds where horseshoe vortices breach surface armor into finer sub-layers ("armor-break" scour, Kabiri-Samani, Fathi & Farooq 2026, DOI 10.2478/johh-2026-0004), across multi-flood deposition-erosion sequences (Link et al. 2020, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)HY.1943-7900.0001696), or when woody debris rafts widen the effective pier obstruction.

spec_plate.division: HYDRAULIC SCOUR / ILLUSTRATIVE MODEL (FILING LABEL · NOT A DESIGN METHOD)
spec_plate.title: Circular Bridge Pier Clear-Water Horseshoe-Vortex Scour & Flood Time-Scale Illustrative Envelope
spec_plate.body: Illustrative closed-form hydraulic study, not a bridge foundation design check (AASHTO LRFD / FHWA HEC-18) or site geotechnical evaluation: models a single unskewed circular concrete pier (a* = 2.00 m, K_1 = 1.0, K_2 = 1.0, K_3 = 1.1) in approach depth y_1 = 3.00 m over uniform cohesionless quartz sand-gravel (d_50 = 2.00 mm, s = 2.65, θ_c = 0.045, u_*c = 0.03817 m/s, V_c = 0.860 m/s, f_1 = 0.8262, f_3 = 0.6263) across clear-water intensities V_1 / V_c ∈ [0.45, 1.00] and flood durations t_d ∈ [2, 240] h. Contraction scour, abutment scour, live-bed dune passage, cohesive clays, graded armor breach, pile-cap exposure, and debris accumulation fall outside this reduced 2-slider curve. Nothing on this page may be used to assess or reduce the design scour depth at a real bridge.
spec_plate.meta: Primary anchors: Buffington 1999 (DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9429(1999)125:4(376)) · Melville 1997 (DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9429(1997)123:2(125)) · Melville & Chiew 1999 (DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9429(1999)125:1(59)) · Sheppard, Melville & Demir 2014 (DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)HY.1943-7900.0000800) · Model values, not field survey data

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE E.16-A · DIMENSIONLESS TIME t* VS. EMPIRICAL DAY-SECOND CONSTANT IN t_e
sidenote_1.body: Melville and Chiew (1999, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9429(1999)125:1(59)) define dimensionless equilibrium time scale t* = V_1 t_e,sec / a*. Dividing t* (a* / V_1) in seconds by 86,400 s/day gives the dimensional prefactors used here, 30.89 days·s^(−1) (equivalent to 2.669 × 10^6 / 86,400 for shallow flow y_1 / a* <= 6) and 48.26 days·s^(−1) (equivalent to 4.170 × 10^6 / 86,400 for deep flow y_1 / a* > 6), requiring a* in meters and V_1 in m/s, with a small 0.18% empirical fit step at y_1 / a* = 6 (30.89 × 6^0.25 = 48.35 vs. 48.26).

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE E.16-B · POST-EQUILIBRIUM CLAMP & ZERO-CROSSING GUARD ON f_2
sidenote_2.body: Two boundary conditions govern numerical evaluation of clear-water scour: first, f_2 = 1 − 1.2 [ln(V_1 / V_c)]^2 crosses zero at V_1 / V_c = exp(−1 / √1.2) ≈ 0.4014, so clear-water sweeps enforce V_1 / V_c >= 0.45 (where f_2 >= 0.2349). Second, at low intensity V_1 / V_c = 0.45, t_e drops to 8.83 days (212.0 h); when peak duration t_d reaches 240.0 h, t_d / 24 exceeds t_e and K_t must clamp at 1.0 rather than evaluating |ln((t_d / 24) / t_e)| past maturity.

skill.name: bridge-pier-scour-timescale
skill.description: AI-agnostic hydraulic engineering skill for Shields critical velocity V_c, Sheppard-Melville and HEC-18 CSU circular pier scour, and Melville-Chiew clear-water flood-duration time-scale factor K_t.
rules: Enforce finite positive pier diameter a*, approach depth y_1, median grain size d_50, gravity g, sediment specific gravity s > 1.0, relative roughness 5.53 y_1 / d_50 > 1.0, and clear-water intensity ratio V_1 / V_c in [0.405, 1.00].

Evaluate Sheppard-Melville clear-water equilibrium scour y_s,SM = 2.5 a* f_1 f_2 f_3 alongside Froude-capped HEC-18 CSU y_s,CSU, keeping grain-coarseness attenuation f_3 active rather than setting f_3 = 1.

Convert dimensionless time scale t* = V_1 t_e,sec / a* using explicit SI inputs (a* in m, V_1 in m/s, empirical factor 30.89 days*s^-1 for y_1 / a* <= 6 or 48.26 days*s^-1 for y_1 / a* > 6) and clamp K_t(t_d) = 1.0 whenever flood duration t_d / 24 >= t_e.

Label transient clear-water scour y_s(t_d) = K_t(t_d) y_s,SM as a Tier T1-T2 illustrative hydraulic hypothesis falsified by live-bed transport (V_1 / V_c > 1), graded armor-layer breach, multi-flood deposition-erosion cycles, cohesive soils, or debris rafts.

State that this is an illustrative single-event model. Design practice uses equilibrium scour depth (FHWA HEC-18); never use K_t or any value from this skill to assess or reduce the design scour depth at a real bridge.

architecture.title: Funicular Thrust Surfaces, Maxwell–Cremona Duals, and 1:5 Nodal Tectonics
architecture.subtitle: How a compression-only stone vault stands when its thrust line stays inside the masonry (Heyman's safe theorem), checked here against the stricter classical middle-third rule (|e| ≤ t/6), with an illustrative 1:5 springer node whose inside surface is modeled as staying above the dew point.

colophon.identifier: A.01 · Vaults & Thermal Nodes
colophon.kernels: 1:50 Section + 1:5 Nodal Loupe
colophon.benchmarks: Model: middle-third rule |e| ≤ t/6 (geometric factor ≥ 3)
colophon.bridge: Illustrative thermal-bridge node (ISO 10211 / ISO 13788 calculation methods)

steps: Stage 1 (Dead-Load Catenary): Under self-weight, the inverted catenary thrust line follows the center line of the vault (e = 0 mm).

Stage 2 (Asymmetric Haunch Load): Live load at the quarter-span shifts the funicular thrust line toward the extrados at the loaded haunch; at the default e = 32 mm the geometric factor is t/(2|e|) = 600/64 = 9.38.
Stage 3 (Maxwell-Cremona Reciprocal Dual): With q = 24 kN/m, L = 18 m and f = 4.5 m, the horizontal ray H = qL²/(8f) = 216.0 kN and the vertical reaction V = qL/2 = 216.0 kN close the force polygon.

Stage 4 (1:5 Springer Node A-04): A load-bearing thermal break with an assumed λ = 0.19 W/(m·K) is modeled as keeping the interior surface at T_si = 16.4 °C, above the dew point T_dew = 9.3 °C of air at 20 °C and 50% RH. T_si is a fixed illustrative value, not a calculated or measured one.

spec_plate.title: Load-Bearing Structural Thermal Break Module (Node A-04)
spec_plate.body: Illustrative specification for a load-bearing thermal-break pad under a masonry vault springer. The compressive design resistance σ_Rd = 45 MPa and thermal conductivity λ = 0.19 W/(m·K) are design assumptions, not data from a tested product; ordinary concrete conducts heat several times better than this.
spec_plate.meta: Design sketch only · no BIM or CAD files are published · not tested or certified to any standard

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.01 · HEYMAN'S SAFE THEOREM (1966)
sidenote_1.body: Jacques Heyman (1966, DOI 10.1016/0020-7683(66)90018-7) applied plastic theory to masonry: if any thrust line in equilibrium with the loads can be found that lies wholly within the masonry, the structure is safe. The middle-third rule |e| ≤ t/6 is an older and stricter condition that keeps the whole joint in compression; this folio uses it as its design target.

skill.name: tectonic-funicular-envelope
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural and structural engineering skill for funicular vault graphic statics (middle-third rule |e| <= t/6 as a design target) and a 1:5 thermal-break node check.
rules: Horizontal Thrust: H = q * L^2 / (8 * f) under uniform line load q across span L and rise f.

Thrust-line check: compute the geometric factor SF = t / (2 * |e|). SF >= 3 means the thrust line is inside the middle third (|e| <= t / 6); SF = 1 means it has reached the edge, where a hinge can form. Report this as a model result, not as proof of safety.

1:5 Springer Thermal Node: check T_si > T_dew and the temperature factor f_Rsi = (T_si - T_e) / (T_i - T_e) defined in ISO 13788. The target f_Rsi >= 0.70 is this folio's own choice, not a requirement of the standard; state T_i, T_e and humidity with every result.

architecture.title: Reciprocal Timber Gridshells (Nexorades), Eccentric Lap Moments, and 1:5 Shear-Block Joinery
architecture.subtitle: Structural kinematics of bolt-free reciprocal timber frames where each beam rests on its neighbor with a vertical step at each lap, converting global shell thrust into localized bending.
architecture.governing_law: M_lap = V_lap a (1 − λ) · τ_d ≤ k_v f_{v,d}

colophon.identifier: A.02 · Reciprocal Timber Gridshells
colophon.kernels: 1:50 Nexorade Bay + 1:5 Notched Lap Joint
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: M_lap = 5.15 kN·m (a = 0.373 m, λ = 0.25) · utilization 0.64 and SF 3.74 are illustrative
colophon.bridge: Reciprocal Load Sharing

steps: Stage 1 (4-Valence Reciprocal Fan): Four GL28h larch members interlock in a pinwheel loop so no more than two members meet at any point.
Stage 2 (Eccentricity-Induced Dome Rise): An assumed vertical offset e_z = 85 mm at each lap joint tilts each member; repeated around the fan, this gives the dome its rise.

Stage 3 (Notch Shear & Bending Check, in the style of EN 1995-1-1): With V_lap = 18.4 kN, λ = 0.25 and an assumed member length L = 1.493 m (a = λL = 0.373 m), M_lap = 18.4 × 0.373 × 0.75 = 5.15 kN·m. The default notch utilization 0.64 is an illustrative baseline rescaled by the sliders below, not a full design check.
Stage 4 (1:5 CNC Dovetail Shear-Block Node): A proposed node in which hardwood beech dowels and EPDM gaskets carry shear without exposed steel plates (design proposal, not tested).

spec_plate.title: GL28h Larch Reciprocal Gridshell Member & Beech Shear-Key Kit (Node A-08)
spec_plate.body: 5-axis CNC-milled glued laminated larch timber with pre-compressed beechwood shear keys and concealed self-tapping full-thread reinforcement screws (f_{m,k} = 28 MPa, f_{v,k} = 3.5 MPa).
spec_plate.meta: Design proposal, not a product · EN 14080 is the glued-laminated timber product standard such members would need to meet

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.02 · SHORT MEMBERS, NOTCHED LAPS
sidenote_1.body: Reciprocal frames let members shorter than the span cover it together (Popovic Larsen 2007, DOI 10.4324/9780080556000). The trade-off is bending and shear at every notch, which EN 1995-1-1 and notch-fracture reviews ask designers to check (Jockwer, Steiger, and Frangi 2014, DOI 10.1061/(ASCE)ST.1943-541X.0000838).

skill.name: reciprocal-timber-nexorade
skill.description: AI-agnostic structural timber engineering skill for reciprocal gridshells (nexorades), engagement ratio kinematics, and Eurocode 5 notched lap joint verification.
rules: Compute reciprocal lap bending moment M_lap = V_lap * a * (1 - lambda_lap) for engagement ratio lambda_lap = a / L.
Verify Eurocode 5 notched joint shear utilization tau_d / (k_v * f_{v,d}) <= 1.0 using effective depth h_eff.
Provide full-thread self-tapping screw reinforcement perpendicular to grain where tension splitting stress exceeds f_{t,90,d}.

architecture.title: Double-Skin Facade Buoyancy Stack Ventilation, Cavity Plumes, and 1:5 Acoustic Damper Louvers
architecture.subtitle: A model of thermosiphon stack draft Δp_stack = ρ_0 g H β ΔT and solar shading position inside multi-story ventilated glass cavities, and how such a facade could reduce cooling loads.
architecture.governing_law: Δp_stack = ρ_0 g H (ΔT / T_ext) · g_tot = 0.11

colophon.identifier: A.03 · Facade Thermodynamics
colophon.kernels: 1:50 Multi-Story Shaft + 1:5 Damper Sill
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: Δp = 3.92 Pa (ρ_0 = 1.2 kg/m³, H = 9.0 m, ΔT = 11.2 K, T_ext ≈ 303 K) · g_tot = 0.11 assumed
colophon.bridge: Buoyancy Convective Clearance

steps: Stage 1 (Solar Shortwave Absorption): An assumed solar irradiance I_sol = 650 W/m² heats the ventilated blind positioned in the outer third of the 600 mm cavity.
Stage 2 (Hydrostatic Buoyancy Pressure Drive): Δp_stack = ρ_0 g H (ΔT / T_ext) = 1.2 × 9.81 × 9.0 × (11.2 / 303) = 3.92 Pa across a 9.0 m two-story shaft (T_ext ≈ 303 K, about 30 °C, assumed).

Stage 3 (Bernoulli Discharge & Damper Loss Balance): Setting Δp = ζ_tot ρ v² / 2 gives v = 0.84 m/s for an assumed total loss coefficient ζ_tot ≈ 9.3 (inlet, outlet louvers and friction). The 142 m³/h per metre of facade assumes an effective free opening of about 0.047 m² per metre.
Stage 4 (1:5 Acoustic Baffle Sill Node A-12): A proposed mineral-wool lined labyrinth damper with a design target of R_w = 46 dB and C_d = 0.62 (targets, not measured).

spec_plate.title: Thermally Broken Double-Skin Curtain Wall & Acoustic Labyrinth Vent (Node A-12)
spec_plate.body: Naturally ventilated box-window facade assembly with motorized micro-perforated aluminum venetian blinds and sound-attenuating intake sill (U_cw = 0.68 W/(m²·K), g_tot = 0.11, R_w = 46 dB).
spec_plate.meta: Design proposal, not a product · EN 13830 is the curtain walling product standard a real system would be tested to

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.03 · BLIND POSITIONING PARADOX
sidenote_1.body: A blind placed close to the inner glazing tends to pass more of its absorbed heat indoors; moving it toward the outer skin lets more of that heat leave with the cavity air. Saelens, Roels and Hens compare strategies for multiple-skin facades (DOI 10.1016/j.buildenv.2006.06.024). The outer-third position here is a design assumption.

skill.name: double-skin-facade-buoyancy
skill.description: AI-agnostic facade engineering and building physics skill for double-skin curtain wall buoyancy stack ventilation, EN ISO 52022-3 g_tot solar factors, and acoustic intake dampers.
rules: Compute buoyancy stack pressure delta_p_stack = rho_0 * g * H * (T_cav - T_ext) / T_ext and mass flow m_dot = rho * A_eff * sqrt(2 * delta_p / zeta_tot).

Calculate total solar energy transmittance g_tot with the EN ISO 52022-3 method; this folio uses its own design target g_tot <= 0.15 when exterior irradiance exceeds 500 W/m^2 (a folio target, not a requirement of the standard).
This folio assumes a cavity depth D >= 500 mm for maintenance access (the folio's own assumption, not a code requirement), or sealed dry-air Closed Cavity Facade (CCF) modules.

architecture.title: From Archigram's Plug-In Megastructures to British High-Tech Exoskeletons: Gerberette Cantilevers, Maxwell Space Frames & Shearing-Layer Pods
architecture.subtitle: How the plug-in ideas of Peter Cook and Ron Herron's 1960s Archigram drawings are widely seen as an influence on the British High-Tech work of Richard Rogers, Renzo Piano, Peter Rice and Norman Foster—and a lever model of the cast-steel gerberette, with replaceable service modules as a proposal.
architecture.governing_law: T_tie = V_p · (a / c) · b − 3j + 6 = s − m · τ_pod ≪ τ_frame

colophon.identifier: A.04 · Archigram to High-Tech Exoskeletons · CSI 05 12 13
colophon.kernels: Gerberette T_tie = V_p(a/c) · Maxwell Rigidity · Shearing Layers
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: T_tie = 4,800 × 1.60 / 6.00 = 1,280 kN (V_p assumed) · SF 3.12 illustrative
colophon.bridge: Long-Life Frame + Replaceable Services ↔ Adaptable Clinical Buildings (a proposal)

steps: Stage 1 (Archigram Plug-In Matrix, 1961–1964): Peter Cook's Plug-In City and Ron Herron's Walking City imagine a long-lived structural frame carrying short-lived clip-on capsules (the 100-year and 15-year lifetimes used here are the folio's illustrative values).

Stage 2 (Pompidou Cast-Steel Gerberette Equilibrium, 1971–1977): In the folio's lever model, an assumed floor reaction V_p = 4,800 kN acts at a = 1.60 m outside the column and is balanced by an exterior tie: T_tie = V_p·(a/c) = 4,800 × 1.60 / 6.00 = 1,280.0 kN at c = 6.00 m. These are teaching values, not the loads of the real building.

Stage 3 (Foster & Rogers High-Tech Mast Suspension, 1978–1986): Norman Foster (HSBC Hong Kong) hangs floors from masts, and Richard Rogers (Lloyd's of London) places service towers and prefabricated service pods outside the main floor plates.

Stage 4 (Brand's Shearing Layers & Replaceable Service Modules): Stewart Brand describes building layers that change at different rates. Keeping services outside the long-life frame could, as a proposal, make it easier to replace clinical or laboratory service modules.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.04-A · ARCHIGRAM TO FOSTER, ROGERS & FUTURE SYSTEMS
sidenote_1.body: Archigram's members taught at architecture schools such as the Architectural Association, and their drawings are widely seen as an influence on British High-Tech. This folio does not document direct teaching links between Archigram and Team 4 (Norman Foster and Richard Rogers) or Jan Kaplický's Future Systems.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.04-B · SPECIFICATION PLATE · CSI 05 12 13 (ARCHITECTURALLY EXPOSED STRUCTURAL STEEL)
sidenote_2.body: Design proposal, not a tested product: cast-steel gerberette brackets with a specified f_y = 355 MPa and Charpy V-notch ≥ 40 J at −20 °C, external stainless-steel tension tie rods, and quick-disconnect service manifolds.

skill.name: archigram-hightech-exoskeleton
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural and structural engineering skill for Archigram Plug-In megastructures, British High-Tech exoskeletons (Foster, Rogers, Piano, Rice), gerberette cantilever statics, Maxwell-Calladine space-frame rigidity, and Stewart Brand shearing layers.
rules: Evaluate cast-steel gerberette cantilever equilibrium: exterior tension tie force T_tie = V_floor * (a / c) and column compression C_col = V_floor * (1 + a / c).
Verify 3D space-frame static and kinematic determinacy via the Maxwell-Calladine matrix index b - 3j + 6 = s - m (ensuring m = 0 internal mechanisms).

Decouple Stewart Brand's 6 Shearing Layers by routing all Services (HVAC, medical gases, cleanroom exhaust, tau = 7-15 yr) on the exterior exoskeleton outside the 48 m column-free Structure (tau = 60-100 yr).

architecture.title: Acoustic Sabin–Eyring Reverberation, Diffusive Coffered Vaults, and Speech Intelligibility (STI ≥ 0.68)
architecture.subtitle: How Wallace Sabine's reverberation law, Carl Eyring's logarithmic absorption, and Manfred Schroeder's prime-sequence coffers can be used to design rooms where speech is easier to understand.

colophon.identifier: A.05 · Architectural Acoustics · CSI 09 84 00
colophon.kernels: T_60,Eyring = 0.62 s (model) · STI = 0.74 (illustrative)
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: V = 2,400 m³, S ≈ 1,075 m², α_bar = 0.44 → Eyring 0.62 s, Sabine 0.82 s
colophon.bridge: Quieter, Clearer Rooms

steps: Stage 1 (Early Window, cf. Bradley 1986, DOI 10.1121/1.393908): Early sound, within about 50 ms, aids speech; C_50 = +4.8 dB is an illustrative estimate.
Stage 2 (Schroeder Diffusion, DOI 10.1121/1.382601): For prime p and design wavelength λ_0 = c/f_0, well depths d_n = (n² mod p)·λ_0/(2p) scatter reflections.
Stage 3 (Perforated Veneer, cf. Maa 1998, DOI 10.1121/1.423870): Maa models micro-perforated panel absorbers; this untested sketch backs 0.8 mm oak veneer with wool (assumed α_bar = 0.44).
Stage 4 (Eyring Decay, DOI 10.1121/1.1915175): For V = 2,400 m³ and S ≈ 1,075 m², Eyring gives 0.62 s (Sabine 0.82 s); STI = 0.74 is a linear estimate, not an MTF value (DOI 10.1121/1.384464).

architecture.title: Net-Zero Water & Greywater Constructed Wetlands: Subsurface Darcy Filtration, UV-C Photolysis and Hot-Water Recirculation (Design Study)
architecture.subtitle: How a modeled subsurface reed bed removes about 95% of greywater BOD_5 outside, while 60 °C recirculation and a 254 nm UV-C reactor are design targets meant to limit growth of opportunistic waterborne bacteria inside.

colophon.identifier: A.06 · Hydro-Tectonics
colophon.kernels: Kadlec-Knight k-C* · Chick-Watson 5.4-Log UV-C
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: 95.1% BOD_5 removal · 5.4-log UV-C design dose
colophon.bridge: Biofilm-Control Plumbing

steps: Stage 1 (Subsurface Horizontal Darcy Filtration): Greywater flows through washed basalt gravel (φ = 0.38, K_s = 120 m/d) with its water level 150 mm below the gravel surface and no open water surface (a 0.80 m deep bed: 0.65 m saturated below a 150 mm dry layer).

Stage 2 (Rhizosphere Biofilm Oxidation): Phragmites root-zone oxygen transfer drives Kadlec-Knight exponential BOD_5 decay from 140 mg/L to 6.8 mg/L (τ = 3.2 d) in the folio model, with the folio's assumed C* = 3.0 mg/L and k = 1.12 per day.

Stage 3 (Dead-Leg-Free 60 °C Potable Recirculation): Copper-silver / stainless manifold designed to target v ≥ 0.6 m/s and T ≥ 60 °C up to every point-of-use mixing valve (design target, not measured).
Stage 4 (254 nm UV-C Photolysis & Thermal Trap Purge): Delivers H = 45 mJ/cm² UV-C fluence (a 5.4-log reduction in the folio's Chick-Watson model) plus self-heating sink traps.

sidenote_2.body: Offset drain clinical washbasin with an automated 65 °C thermal P-trap cycle, intended to reduce droplet dispersal from the drain. Kotay et al. (2017, DOI 10.1128/AEM.03327-16) modeled sink-trap dispersal with a marker organism; this fixture is a design proposal and has not been tested.

rules: Size subsurface horizontal-flow wetlands via Darcy's law Q = K_s A_c S and Kadlec-Knight kinetics C_out = C* + (C_in - C*) exp(-k_v * tau).
This folio's own design target (not a standard or a clinical requirement): potable hot-water recirculation >= 60 C at velocity >= 0.6 m/s, with no stagnant dead-legs.

Apply the folio's design targets of a 4-log model reduction (254 nm UV-C fluence H >= 34 mJ/cm^2 at 0.12 log per mJ/cm^2) and non-splashing offset drains; report log reductions as model values, never as measured outcomes.
