architecture.title: Luis Barragán's Chromatic Tectonics, Kubelka–Munk Pigment Radiosity & Emotional Spatial Wavefields
architecture.subtitle: How Luis Barragán and Jesús 'Chucho' Reyes Ferreira worked with saturated color (Rosa Mexicano, cobalt blue, ochre) and Mexican daylight (Zanco 2001), alongside Josef Albers's color relativity (1963)—modeled here via Kubelka–Munk scattering (DOI 10.1364/JOSA.38.000448) and diffuse radiosity (Goral et al. 1984, DOI 10.1145/800031.808601).

colophon.identifier: A.07 · Barragán Chromatic Tectonics & Radiosity · CSI 09 24 00
colophon.kernels: Kubelka–Munk Two-Flux Law · Fredholm Diffuse Radiosity
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: R_∞ = 0.389 at K/S = 0.48 · +31.1% bounce gain at F_12 = 0.61 (illustrative)
colophon.bridge: Barragán Mineral Stucco Radiosity ↔ P.08 Thin-Film Car Paint & M.08 Color Geodesics

steps: Stage 1 (Corridor Spectral Filtering, λ ≈ 582 nm): In Casa Gilardi (1976; Coelho 2015, DOI 10.4000/ambiances.606), daylight passing yellow glazing loses short-wave blue light; about 582 nm is an illustrative dominant wavelength.

Stage 2 (Kubelka–Munk Scattering): For K/S = 0.48, Kubelka's infinite-thickness equation (1948, DOI 10.1364/JOSA.38.000448) gives R_∞ = 1 + K/S − √((K/S)² + 2 K/S) = 0.389, assuming a matte Lambertian layer.

Stage 3 (Enclosure Inter-Reflection): Following the diffuse radiosity balance (Goral et al. 1984, DOI 10.1145/800031.808601), a one-parameter enclosure series with effective return factor F_12 = 0.61 gives gain 1 / (1 − R_∞ F_12) − 1 ≈ +31.1% (multiplier 1.311) at R_∞ = 0.389—an illustrative model value, not a measured color shift.

Stage 4 (Torres de Satélite Parallax & Albers Contrast): Built by Barragán and Mathias Goeritz (1957–58; Pelletier 2008, DOI 10.1111/j.1531-314X.2008.00234.x), the towers—the tallest about 52 m—shift silhouette from moving cars while juxtaposed planes illustrate relational contrast (Albers 1963).

spec_plate.title: Slaked Lime Stucco & Mineral Pigment Wash (Design Proposal)
spec_plate.body: Three-coat slaked calcium-hydroxide lime plaster (Ca(OH)2 carbonating to CaCO3 calcite; Cultrone et al. 2005, DOI 10.1016/j.cemconres.2004.12.012) with porous vapor permeability (Parra-Fernández & Varas-Muriel 2025, DOI 10.3989/mc.2025.379124; hydraulic lime permeability in Isebaert et al. 2016, DOI 10.1617/s11527-016-0829-1) and mineral oxide pigments.
spec_plate.meta: Design proposal · K/S = 0.48 and 85° gloss < 2 GU are targets, not measurements

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.07-A · BARRAGÁN, CHUCHO REYES & TORRES DE SATÉLITE
sidenote_1.body: Painter and collector Jesús 'Chucho' Reyes Ferreira influenced Luis Barragán's palette (Zanco 2001). Torres de Satélite (1957–58), by Barragán and Mathias Goeritz, stands beside a highway for moving viewers; the tallest tower rises about 52 m (Pelletier 2008, DOI 10.1111/j.1531-314X.2008.00234.x).

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.07-B · SPECIFICATION PLATE · CSI 09 24 00 / CARBONATED LIME
sidenote_2.body: Unlike film-forming acrylic paints, carbonated lime plaster builds a porous CaCO3 calcite network (Cultrone et al. 2005, DOI 10.1016/j.cemconres.2004.12.012) that transmits water vapor (Parra-Fernández & Varas-Muriel 2025, DOI 10.3989/mc.2025.379124) and scatters light isotropically via Kubelka–Munk transfer (DOI 10.1364/JOSA.38.000448).

skill.name: barragan-kubelka-munk-radiosity
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural daylighting and color-physics skill for Luis Barragan chromatic tectonics, Kubelka-Munk pigment reflectance, and Fredholm diffuse radiosity.
rules: Compute infinite-thickness Kubelka-Munk diffuse reflectance R_inf = 1 + (K/S) - sqrt((K/S)^2 + 2*(K/S)) from absorption K and scattering S (Kubelka 1948, DOI 10.1364/JOSA.38.000448).

Solve wavelength-resolved diffuse radiosity B_i(lambda) = E_i(lambda) + rho_i(lambda) * sum_j F_ij * B_j(lambda) across 380-780 nm (Goral et al. 1984, DOI 10.1145/800031.808601; Ruppertsberg & Bloj 2008, DOI 10.3758/BRM.40.1.304).

Specify matte, vapor-permeable lime plaster (Cultrone et al. 2005, DOI 10.1016/j.cemconres.2004.12.012; Parra-Fernández & Varas-Muriel 2025, DOI 10.3989/mc.2025.379124) with an unmeasured 85-degree gloss < 2 GU target so diffuse bounce dominates over specular glare.

architecture.title: AI-Designed Daytime Radiative Sky-Cooling Photonic Roofs (8–13 μm Window) & Stefan Phase-Change Envelopes
architecture.subtitle: A building-physics model pairing daytime radiative sky cooling across the 8–13 μm atmospheric window (Raman et al. 2014, DOI 10.1038/nature13883; Mandal et al. 2018, DOI 10.1126/science.aat9513) with a proposed Stefan phase-change ceiling buffer (Carslaw & Jaeger 1959; Kuznik et al. 2011, DOI 10.1016/j.rser.2010.08.019).
architecture.governing_law: P_net = P_rad(T) − P_atm(T_a) − (1 − R_sol)I_sol − h_c(T_a − T) · s(t) = 2λ_s√(α t) · CSI 07 54 00

colophon.identifier: A.08 · Photonic Sky-Cooling & Stefan PCM · CSI 07 54 00
colophon.kernels: Planck 8–13 μm Sky Window · Stefan Moving-Boundary PCM Storage
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: R_solar = 97.0% · ε_LWIR = 95.0% · P_net = +86.4 W/m² (−6.2 °C)
colophon.bridge: Passive Sub-Ambient Sky Cooling ↔ Cooler Storage Rooms (Open Question, Not Medical Cold Storage)

steps: Stage 1 (Solar Reflection, 0.3–2.5 μm): In the model the roof reflects 97.0% of an assumed 1,000 W/m² of midday sunlight, absorbing (1 − 0.97) × 1,000 = 30 W/m² (Raman et al. 2014, DOI 10.1038/nature13883, report about 97% solar reflection).

Stage 2 (Emission in the 8–13 μm Window): Through the 8–13 μm atmospheric transparency window (Catalanotti et al. 1975, DOI 10.1016/0038-092X(75)90062-6; Granqvist & Hjortsberg 1981, DOI 10.1063/1.329270), the model assigns an illustrative net radiative sky exchange of about 116.4 W/m² at air temperature.

Stage 3 (Sub-Ambient Equilibrium Below Air Temperature): Net cooling power is P_net = 116.4 − 30 = +86.4 W/m². Dividing by an assumed combined heat-exchange coefficient of about 13.9 W/(m²·K) gives a model roof surface about 6.2 °C below outdoor air under the stated assumptions (Raman et al. 2014, DOI 10.1038/nature13883, measured about 4.9 °C and 40.1 W/m²).

Stage 4 (Stefan Phase-Change Thermal Ceiling Buffer): A proposed 21 °C PCM ceiling panel could absorb indoor heat along a moving melting front s(t) = 2λ_s√(α t) (Carslaw & Jaeger 1959; Kuznik et al. 2011, DOI 10.1016/j.rser.2010.08.019). The panel is an untested design proposal and was not sized here.

spec_plate.title: Microporous PVDF-HFP Radiative Sky-Cooling Membrane & Bio-PCM Thermal Ceiling
spec_plate.body: Untested design proposal: a hierarchically porous poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) cool-roof coating of the kind reported by Mandal et al. (2018, DOI 10.1126/science.aat9513), with assumed R_solar = 0.97 and ε_8-13um = 0.95, paired with 21 °C PCM ceiling cassettes (Kuznik et al. 2011, DOI 10.1016/j.rser.2010.08.019).
spec_plate.meta: References: Raman et al. 2014 (DOI 10.1038/nature13883); Granqvist & Hjortsberg 1981 (DOI 10.1063/1.329270) · Model estimates, not measurements · ASTM E1980 defines solar reflectance index; none was calculated here

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.08-A · VISIBLE STRUCTURAL COLOR WITHOUT SOLAR HEATING
sidenote_1.body: A white roof can glare. Chen et al. (2020, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aaz5413) report paintable bilayer coatings in which a thin top layer absorbs narrowly for visible color while a scattering underlayer reflects near-infrared sunlight. Because visible absorption adds solar heat, colored roofs may cool less than white ones; this folio models white-limit assumptions only.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.08-B · SPECIFICATION PLATE · CSI 07 54 00 / STEFAN NUMBER
sidenote_2.body: Illustrative storage estimate: about 7.2 kg/m² of PCM with latent heat L_f = 210 kJ/kg stores 1,512 kJ/m² (420 Wh/m²), assuming about half of an 18 mm panel is PCM and Stefan number Ste = c_p ΔT / L_f = 0.085 (Carslaw & Jaeger 1959; Kuznik et al. 2011, DOI 10.1016/j.rser.2010.08.019). No chiller-demand estimate is computed here.

skill.name: radiative-sky-cooling-stefan-pcm
skill.description: AI-agnostic building-physics and photonic-envelope skill for daytime radiative sky cooling across the 8-13 um atmospheric window and Stefan phase-change thermal storage.
rules: Evaluate net radiative cooling flux P_net(T) = epsilon_LWIR * sigma * T^4 - P_atm(T_amb) - (1 - R_solar) * I_solar - h_c * (T_amb - T).

Treat R_solar >= 0.94 across 0.3-2.5 um and epsilon_LWIR >= 0.90 across 8-13 um as this folio's own design targets under I_solar = 1000 W/m^2; report P_net and Delta T as model estimates, not measured results.
Compute Stefan phase-change melting front depth s(t) = 2 * lambda_s * sqrt(alpha_th * t) where lambda_s * exp(lambda_s^2) * erf(lambda_s) = Ste / sqrt(pi).

architecture.title: Bending-Active & Hygroscopic Programmable Timber Skins: Timoshenko Bilayer Curvature, Orthotropic Moisture Swelling & Zero-Energy Climate Facades
architecture.subtitle: Completing the timber-and-climate thread of Folios A.02, E.04, and A.08: how Stephen Timoshenko's bilayer curvature formula describes wood bilayers that bend with humidity, the idea behind the motor-free facade skins studied at ICD/ITKE Stuttgart. A design model.

colophon.identifier: A.09 · Hygroscopic Timber Skins & Timoshenko Curvature · CSI 06 18 00
colophon.kernels: Timoshenko Bilayer Curvature · Orthotropic Wood Sorption (α_T vs. α_L)
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: ΔMC = +6.0% · h = 6.0 mm · m = 2 · n = 10.6 ⇒ κ = 1.42 m⁻¹ · δ_tip = 128 mm
colophon.bridge: Completes A.02/E.04 · Wood Cell-Wall Swelling

steps: Stage 1 (Orthotropic Cell-Wall Sorption, Continuing E.04): Below fiber saturation (about 28% MC), the model assumes beech swells tangentially at α_T = 0.32%/%MC and along the grain at only α_L = 0.012%/%MC. Both coefficients are assumed round values.

Stage 2 (Timoshenko Bilayer Formula, DOI 10.1364/JOSA.11.000233): Bonding an active tangential ply h_2 to a passive longitudinal ply h_1 turns the misfit strain Δε = (α_T − α_L)ΔMC = 0.0185 into curvature. With the folio's assumed m = h_1/h_2 = 2 and n = E_1/E_2 = 10.6 the geometry factor is 0.46 and κ = 1.42 m⁻¹. Equal plies of equal stiffness (m = n = 1) would give 4.62 m⁻¹.

Stage 3 (Weather-Responsive Facade Petal, Model): A 425 mm cantilever petal moves δ_tip ≈ ½ κ L² = 128 mm at the tip as it dries. The 64.5% free vent area is a fixed illustrative value, not computed from the geometry. Rain-tightness was not assessed.

Stage 4 (Self-Shaping CLT, Continuing A.02): Wood et al. (2020) describe curved cross-laminated timber components for the Urbach Tower that took their shape during drying instead of being milled or pressed to a curve.

spec_plate.title: Programmable Hygroscopic European Beech Bilayer Climate Envelope & Self-Shaping CLT
spec_plate.body: Design proposal: cross-grained Fagus sylvatica (European beech) bilayer facade elements bonded with a one-component polyurethane structural adhesive, a weather coat, and stainless limit stops. Not a tested product.
spec_plate.meta: References: Timoshenko (1925) DOI 10.1364/JOSA.11.000233; Reichert, Menges & Correa (2015) DOI 10.1016/j.cad.2014.02.010 · Model values; no cycle testing was done

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.09-A · COMPLETING FOLIO A.02 TIMBER MECHANICS WITH TIMOSHENKO (1925)
sidenote_1.body: Timoshenko's dimensionless geometry factor f(m, n) peaks when stiffness-weighted layer thicknesses satisfy E_1 h_1² = E_2 h_2², maximizing autonomous curvature per unit thickness h.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.09-B · SPECIFICATION PLATE · CSI 06 18 00 (PROGRAMMABLE WOOD)
sidenote_2.body: By choosing grain orientations in each layer, a flat timber panel can be made to curve as it dries. Single-curved components have been built this way (Wood et al. 2020); doubly curved shells made the same way are a proposal here.

skill.name: hygroscopic-timber-timoshenko-bilayer
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural and timber-engineering skill for Stephen Timoshenko bilayer curvature, orthotropic wood moisture swelling (alpha_T vs alpha_L), and zero-energy responsive building skins.
rules: Compute differential hygroscopic strain Delta_epsilon = (alpha_T - alpha_L) * Delta_MC below the Fiber Saturation Point (MC <= 28%).
Evaluate Timoshenko curvature kappa = 6 * (1 + m)^2 * Delta_epsilon / (h * (3 * (1 + m)^2 + (1 + m*n) * (m^2 + 1/(m*n)))) with m = h_1/h_2 and n = E_1/E_2.

Calculate cantilever aperture tip deflection delta_tip = (1 - cos(kappa * L)) / kappa approx 0.5 * kappa * L^2, state the m and n used, and check rolling shear against the timber code that applies; report results as model values.

colophon.kernels: Miura-Ori Spherical Vertex Law · Schenk–Guest Auxetic ν_xy = −tan² φ
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: α = 64° · θ = 36° ⇒ ν_xy ≈ −0.37 (folio parametrization) · SHGC = 0.19 (assumed SHGC_glass = 0.60, η_shade = 0.845)
colophon.bridge: Completes A.04/A.03/M.05

steps: Stage 1 (Kawasaki & Maekawa Flat-Foldable Vertex, Continuing M.05): Four rigid parallelogram facets meet at a degree-4 vertex satisfying Kawasaki alternating-angle sums (π) and Maekawa mountain-valley parity (|M − V| = 2; Hull 2020, DOI 10.1017/9781108778633), leaving one degree of freedom in the ideal rigid sheet (Miura 1985).

Stage 2 (Spherical Trigonometry Dihedral Coupling): With primary fold angle γ_1 = θ = 36° and α = 64°, tan(γ_2/2) = cos α · tan(γ_1/2) yields secondary fold angle γ_2 ≈ 16.2° for zero-thickness facets (real thick panels require hinge-offset geometry; Tachi 2011, DOI 10.1201/b10971-24).

Stage 3 (Auxetic Poisson Ratio, after Schenk & Guest 2013, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1217998110): Schenk and Guest showed that a Miura-ori sheet exhibits a negative in-plane Poisson ratio. In this folio's simplified parametrization, cos φ = sin α · cos(θ/2) gives φ ≈ 31.3° and ν_xy = −tan² φ ≈ −0.37 at default settings.

Stage 4 (Mashrabiya-Inspired Solar Shading, Continuing A.03/A.04): With assumed bare-glazing SHGC_glass = 0.60 and shading effectiveness η_shade = 0.845, the folio's illustrative rule SHGC = SHGC_glass · (1 − η_shade · cos θ) gives 0.19 at θ = 36° (−68.4% solar heat gain in the model); published origami facade simulations (Meloni et al. 2023, DOI 10.1016/j.scs.2023.104740; Kahramanoğlu & Çakıcı Alp 2023, DOI 10.1016/j.jobe.2023.106241) motivate this study, though cooling loads and daylight are not computed here.

This folio does not estimate building cooling-energy savings; those depend on climate, glazing, and orientation, and any assembly remains untested.

skill.name: kinetic-origami-miura-facade
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural and mechanical-metamaterial skill for Miura-ori rigid origami kinematics, Kawasaki flat-foldability, Schenk-Guest negative Poisson ratio (nu_xy = -tan^2(phi)), and kinetic solar facades.
rules: Enforce Kawasaki's flat-foldability theorem sum(alpha_even) = sum(alpha_odd) = pi and Maekawa's mountain-valley rule |M - V| = 2 at every interior degree-4 vertex (Hull 2020, DOI 10.1017/9781108778633).

Compute the semi-width angle phi from this folio's simplified parametrization cos(phi) = sin(alpha) * cos(theta / 2) and evaluate nu_xy = -tan^2(phi) < 0 (about -0.37 at alpha = 64, theta = 36); note that Schenk & Guest (2013, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1217998110) parametrize the fold differently.

Couple facade deployment angle theta to solar altitude; treat SHGC <= 0.22 at peak insolation and >= 250 EML daylight as this folio's own design targets and report SHGC as a model value, not a measurement.

colophon.identifier: A.11 · 3D Polyhedral Graphic Statics & Passive Sky-Cooling Vaults · REV 1.5
colophon.kernels: Maxwell–Rankine Dual Polyhedra (Γ ↔ Γ^*) · Airy Concavity det(H_Φ) > 0 · 8–13 μm Sky-Cooling
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: det(H_Φ) = +1.84 (illustrative) · q_net = 98.4 W/m² at air temperature · ΔT_eq = −7.08 °C for an assumed 13.9 W/(m²·K)
colophon.bridge: Continues A.01/A.02 ↔ Toolbox X.03 STEP AP242 · Concave Stress Vaults & P(VdF-HFP) Sky-Cooling

steps: Stage 1 (Airy Stress Function & Negative-Definite Hessian): In-plane membrane stresses are written through an Airy stress function Φ(x, y) as σ_xx = Φ_yy, σ_yy = Φ_xx, σ_xy = −Φ_xy. In his 1870 paper on reciprocal figures Maxwell read a polyhedron lifted over a frame as a discrete stress function of this kind.

Stage 2 (Rankine–Minkowski Reciprocal Polyhedra Γ ↔ Γ^*): In 3D polyhedral graphic statics (Akbarzadeh, Van Mele & Block 2015, DOI 10.1016/j.cad.2015.01.006), each member of the form diagram is perpendicular to a face of a closed cell in the force diagram, and the face area is proportional to the member force; a closed cell means the forces at that node balance.

Stage 3 (Concavity and Compression): If the Hessian of Φ is negative-definite (Φ_xx < 0, Φ_yy < 0, det(H_Φ) = Φ_xx Φ_yy − Φ_xy² > 0), the in-plane stress field of the model is compressive everywhere. That is a property of the model under the load case considered, not a structural check of a real shell; the 52 mm thickness is an illustrative value.

Stage 4 (8–13 μm Radiative Sky-Cooling Extrados & Toolbox X.03 CAD Bridge): With a porous P(VdF-HFP)-type coating (Mandal et al. 2018, DOI 10.1126/science.aat9513) assumed at R_solar = 0.96 under 890 W/m² of sun, the extrados absorbs 35.6 W/m². The model assigns a net radiative exchange with the sky of 134.0 W/m² at air temperature (a fixed illustrative value), so q_net = 134.0 − 35.6 = 98.4 W/m²; divided by an assumed combined heat-exchange coefficient of 13.9 W/(m²·K), that gives ΔT_eq ≈ −7.08 °C. Toolbox X.03 provides the STEP AP242 voussoir geometry.

spec_plate.body: Design proposal: compression-only tile and dry-cut stone funicular vaults shaped with reciprocal polyhedra (tools such as compas-dev/compas, geometry from Toolbox X.03), with a porous P(VdF-HFP)-type sky-cooling coating on the extrados at assumed R_solar = 0.96 and ε_8-13μm = 0.95. spec_plate.meta: References: Akbarzadeh et al. 2015, DOI 10.1016/j.cad.2015.01.006 · Raman et al. 2014, DOI 10.1038/nature13883 · Mandal et al. 2018, DOI 10.1126/science.aat9513 · Model values, not measurements

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.11-A · CROSS-FIELD ANALOGY · SOAP FOAM & GUASTAVINO TILE VAULTS
sidenote_1.body: Rafael Guastavino and his son, who emigrated from Spain to the United States in 1881, built hundreds of thin timbrel tile vaults there (López et al. 2023, DOI 10.3390/buildings13082052). 3D polyhedral graphic statics came more than a century later, so it played no part in their designs. The soap-foam picture is this folio's analogy: in a polyhedral force diagram each cell closes, much as each bubble in a foam is closed, and each face area is proportional to the force in the matching member.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.11-B · DAYTIME SKY-COOLING VAULTS & TOOLBOX X.03 CAD
sidenote_2.body: Mandal et al. (2018, DOI 10.1126/science.aat9513) reported porous P(VdF-HFP) coatings that reached about 6 °C below ambient under 890 W/m² of sun and about 96 W/m² of cooling power under 750 W/m². In this folio's model the same kind of coating on a vault extrados gives 98.4 W/m² at air temperature, a model value. The companion 7-voussoir STEP AP242 and GLB kit is in Toolbox X.03 (/toolchain/x03/).

skill.name: 3d-polyhedral-graphic-statics
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural and structural skill for 3D Polyhedral Graphic Statics (Maxwell-Rankine dual polyhedra), strictly concave Airy stress surfaces, 8-13 um daytime radiative sky-cooling vault envelopes, and Toolbox X.03 STEP AP242 voussoir coupling.
rules: Check 3D nodal equilibrium by requiring every polyhedral cell c_v^* in the reciprocal force diagram Gamma^* to close within a numerical tolerance (for example ||sum F_i|| < 1e-12 kN).

Check that the model stress field is compressive by testing the Airy stress Hessian: Phi_xx < 0, Phi_yy < 0, and det(H_Phi) = Phi_xx*Phi_yy - Phi_xy^2 > 0. This is a model check for one load case, not a structural assessment of a real vault.

Evaluate daytime radiative sky-cooling net flux q_net = q_rad(T_s) - q_atm(T_a) - q_solar*(1 - R_solar) - h_c*(T_a - T_s); treat q_net >= 80 W/m^2 at T_a = 303.15 K and Delta T_eq <= -4.5 C as this folio's own design targets, and report results as model values, never as measurements.

architecture.subtitle: Synthesizing Folio A.04's lightweight megastructures, A.08's 8–13 μm radiative sky cooling, and A.10's deployable skins: a design study of how the floating-compression tensegrity of Kenneth Snelson and Buckminster Fuller could carry a radiative sky-cooling membrane over a civic canopy.
architecture.governing_law: A t = f · K_T = K_E + K_G(t_0) ≻ 0 · P_cool = P_rad(T_s) − P_atm(T_amb) − P_sun

colophon.identifier: A.12 · Tensegrity Cable-Strut Domes & 8–13 μm Sky-Cooling Canopies · ASCE 19
colophon.kernels: Pellegrino–Calladine SVD Nullspace (s ≥ 1, m ≥ 0) · Geometric Stiffness K_G(t_0) · Raman 8–13 μm
colophon.benchmarks: Model values: t_0 = 185 kN · q_net = 98.4 W/m² at air temperature ⇒ ΔT ≈ −5.2 °C for an assumed 18.9 W/(m²·K)
colophon.bridge: Synthesizes A.04/A.08/A.10 · Analogy: cellular tensegrity hypothesis (Ingber 1993) ↔ prestressed cable domes

steps: Stage 1 (Snelson–Fuller Islands of Compression in an Ocean of Tension): Isolated steel compression struts float without touching one another, suspended inside a continuous prestressed cable net (Calladine 1978, DOI 10.1016/0020-7683(78)90052-5).

Stage 2 (Pellegrino–Calladine Equilibrium Matrix SVD): Singular Value Decomposition of the equilibrium matrix A (Pellegrino & Calladine 1986, DOI 10.1016/0020-7683(86)90014-4) identifies s = dim ker(A) self-stress states and m = dim ker(Aᵀ) infinitesimal mechanisms.

Stage 3 (Geometric Prestress Stiffening K_G(t_0) ≻ 0): Just as tightening a guitar string raises its pitch, cable prestress t_0 makes the geometric stiffness matrix K_G(t_0) positive on the mechanism modes, so the prestressed structure is stiff in the model. The structural mass figure of 12.4 kg/m² shown on this page is illustrative, not a design result.

Stage 4 (Daytime Radiative Sky-Cooling Membrane Canopy, Continuing A.08): The membrane is assumed to reflect 97% of an assumed 1,000 W/m² of sunlight, as the photonic surface of Raman et al. did (2014, DOI 10.1038/nature13883), so it absorbs 30 W/m². The model assigns a net radiative exchange with the sky of 128.4 W/m² at air temperature, a fixed illustrative value, so q_net = 128.4 − 30 = 98.4 W/m². Divided by an assumed combined heat-exchange coefficient of about 18.9 W/(m²·K), that gives a membrane surface about 5.2 °C below the air in the model.

spec_plate.title: Geiger–Levy Cable-Strut Tensegrity Domes with Photonic Radiative Sky-Cooling PTFE Cladding
spec_plate.body: Design proposal: a Geiger-type circular cable dome, prestressed so that its geometric stiffness K_G(t_0) is positive on its mechanism modes, clad in a microporous radiative sky-cooling membrane. Not an engineered or tested assembly; NREL/EnergyPlus is named as a tool a reader could use, and this folio ran no simulation.
spec_plate.meta: References: Pellegrino & Calladine (1986) DOI 10.1016/0020-7683(86)90014-4 · Raman et al. (2014) DOI 10.1038/nature13883 · ASCE 19 is the standard for structural applications of steel cables; it sets none of this folio's values

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.12-A · CROSS-FIELD ANALOGY · BICYCLE WHEELS, LIVING CELLS & THE SAHARAN SILVER ANT
sidenote_1.body: A bicycle wheel is stiff because its thin spokes are pretensioned, so they never have to carry compression. Donald Ingber proposed that living cells use a similar tensegrity principle in their cytoskeleton (1993, DOI 10.1242/jcs.104.3.613). Saharan silver ants are covered in hairs that raise their near-infrared reflection and help them shed heat by thermal radiation (Shi et al. 2015, DOI 10.1126/science.aab3564). Joining a tensegrity dome to a radiative-cooling skin is this folio's design idea.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.12-B · OPEN-SOURCE BUILDING PHYSICS · NREL/ENERGYPLUS & COMPAS
sidenote_2.body: Open tools such as compas-dev/compas (for equilibrium matrices and form finding) and NREL/EnergyPlus (for whole-building energy) could be used to test a canopy like this one. This folio ran neither. A cooler membrane is not a heat-safety measure, and nothing here is guidance on protecting people during heatwaves.

skill.name: tensegrity-nullspace-skycooling
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural engineering skill for Pellegrino-Calladine tensegrity equilibrium matrix SVD (s = dim ker(A), m = dim ker(A^T)), geometric prestress stiffening K_G(t_0), and 8-13 um radiative sky-cooling membranes.
rules: Compute Singular Value Decomposition of equilibrium matrix A to extract self-stress vector t_0 in ker(A) with strictly positive tension in all cables.
Verify first-order prestress stability by checking u^T * K_G(t_0) * u > 0 for all inextensional mechanism modes u in ker(A^T).
Evaluate net daytime radiative cooling flux q_net = P_rad(T_s) - P_atm(T_amb) - (1 - R_solar) * I_sun across the 8-13 um atmospheric window.

architecture.subtitle: Continuing Folio A.01's 2D catenary thrust lines and A.11's 3D polyhedral force diagrams: a structural design study of Heinz Isler's physical form-finding—inverted hanging cloth, pneumatic membranes, and sculpted hills—coupled to an idealized spherical-cap model (31.6 m span, 4.2 m rise, 90 mm thickness) comparing Zoelly classical buckling against an illustrative imperfection-sensitivity knockdown curve.
architecture.governing_law: R = (L² + 4f²)/(8f) · σ_mem = q R / (2t) · p_cr^cl = 2E / √(3(1−ν²)) · (t/R)² · p_cr^act = γ_kd · p_cr^cl

colophon.identifier: A.13 · Heinz Isler Funicular Thin-Shell Domes & Imperfection Knockdowns · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: Inverted-Hanging Membrane Analogy · Zoelly Classical Shell Buckling · Imperfection Knockdown Curve
colophon.benchmarks: Idealized spherical-cap model: L = 31.6 m · f = 4.2 m · R = 31.82 m · t = 90.0 mm · σ_mem = 0.587 MPa · p_cr^cl = 282.9 kN/m² · γ_kd = 0.189 · p_cr^act = 53.4 kN/m² · λ_b = 16.1
colophon.bridge: Continues A.01/A.11 · Idealized spherical-cap stability model vs. free-edge shell form-finding

steps: Stage 1 (Inverted-Hanging Cloth & Pneumatic Form-Finding): In his 1959 IASS Madrid lecture (published 1961), Swiss engineer Heinz Isler grouped thin concrete shell form-finding into three physical experiments: freely shaped hills, inflated pneumatic membranes, and hanging textiles stiffened with plaster or frozen in winter air and inverted. Because a hanging sheet carries gravity load in pure membrane tension, its inverted rigid geometry channels uniform dead load along compression-only trajectories with minimal bending.

Stage 2 (Idealized Spherical-Cap Geometry & Uniform-Projection Membrane Stress): As a tractable analytical reference—distinct from Deitingen Süd's three-point free-edge wing shells, which share only the 90 mm double-rebar-cover thickness—the model evaluates a spherical cap of span L = 31.6 m and rise f = 4.2 m (curvature radius R = 31.82 m, rim half-angle φ_0 = 29.8°). At t = 90.0 mm (ρ = 2,400 kg/m³) plus 1.20 kN/m² superimposed load, uniform plan-projected gravity load is q = 3.318 kN/m² (neglecting the sec φ_0 = 1.152 slope factor at the rim and boundary haunches), giving crown compressive stress σ_mem = 0.587 MPa.

Stage 3 (Zoelly Classical Elastic Buckling & Post-Buckling Sensitivity): Because σ_mem = 0.587 MPa is under 2% of an assumed 35 MPa concrete compressive strength, crushing does not govern this model. Instead, thin doubly curved shells face elastic snap-through buckling. R. Zoelly's 1915 linear-elastic formula for an ideal uniform sphere under normal pressure gives p_cr^cl = 282.9 kN/m² at E = 30.0 GPa and ν = 0.20—an idealized upper bound that omits concrete creep, cracking (Ramm & Mehlhorn 1991, DOI 10.1016/0141-0296(91)90050-M), asymmetric snow, and edge bending.

Stage 4 (Illustrative Knockdown Curve & Tier T2 Hypothesis): Hutchinson (1967, DOI 10.1115/1.3607667), Gerasimidis et al. (2018, DOI 10.1115/1.4040455), and Abbasi, Derveni, and Reis (2023, DOI 10.1115/1.4056801) analyzed why tiny inward dimples sharply cut spherical shell buckling capacity below Zoelly's line. Applying an illustrative empirical-style knockdown function γ_kd = 0.14 + 0.32 exp(−0.1 √(R/t)) (NASA SP-8007 and Dulácska inspired, not a design code formula) at R/t = 353.5 yields γ_kd = 0.189, p_cr^act = 53.4 kN/m², and buckling ratio λ_b = 16.1. Hypothesis (Tier T2 model): elastic snap-through under inward dimples governs reserve rather than crushing; falsified for a physical shell if creep, cracking, asymmetric snow, or deeper inward dimples (δ_0 / t > 0.5) push collapse below λ_b = 3.0 or induce edge bending.

spec_plate.division: CSI MASTERFORMAT 03 31 00 / 03 38 00 / ACI 334R CONCRETE SHELL DESIGN STUDY
spec_plate.title: Idealized Funicular Spherical-Cap Shell Model (90 mm Crown Reference)
spec_plate.body: Analytical design study of an idealized spherical cap (L = 31.6 m, f = 4.2 m, R = 31.82 m, t = 90.0 mm) comparing Zoelly classical elastic buckling against an illustrative imperfection knockdown curve. Inspired by Heinz Isler's 90 mm double-rebar-cover Deitingen Süd shells, whose three-point free-edge geometry is more complex than a spherical cap. Model values only; not an engineered structural drawing or construction specification.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.13-A · DEITINGEN SÜD (1968) & THE 90 MM COVER DETAIL
sidenote_1.body: Heinz Isler's Deitingen Süd motorway canopies in Switzerland (1968) span 31.6 m across triangular wing shells supported on three points without edge beams (Tang 2015, DOI 10.1260/0266-3511.30.1.1). Their 90 mm thickness was set largely by construction durability—providing 20 mm concrete cover around double-layer reinforcement—rather than compressive crushing limits. Unlike our simplified spherical-cap benchmark, those free-edge wings rely on three-dimensional hanging-cloth curvature and upturned edge stiffening.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.13-B · INWARD DIMPLES VS. OUTWARD BUMPS (ABBASI ET AL. 2023)
sidenote_2.body: Flat plates hold post-buckling reserve after initial wrinkling, whereas doubly curved compression shells can snap inward suddenly when localized defects seed a dimple. Hutchinson (1967, DOI 10.1115/1.3607667) quantified this steep imperfection sensitivity, Gerasimidis et al. (2018, DOI 10.1115/1.4040455) examined localized dimples versus lateral probes, and Abbasi, Derveni, and Reis (2023, DOI 10.1115/1.4056801) showed that inward dimples cut spherical buckling strength more sharply than outward bumps of matching size.

skill.name: isler-thin-shell-buckling
skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural engineering skill for idealized thin spherical-cap membrane stress, Zoelly (1915) classical elastic buckling, and illustrative imperfection-sensitivity knockdown bounds.
rules: Compute spherical-cap curvature radius R = (L^2 + 4 * f^2) / (8 * f) and uniform-projection crown membrane stress sigma_mem = (q * R) / (2 * t); record the rim slope factor sec(phi_0) omitted by uniform plan projection.
Compute Zoelly (1915) classical elastic buckling pressure p_cr^cl = (2 * E / sqrt(3 * (1 - nu^2))) * (t / R)^2 and verify quadratic (t/R)^2 scaling when thickness doubles.

Apply an explicit empirical-style knockdown function gamma_kd(R/t) = 0.14 + 0.32 * exp(-0.1 * sqrt(R / t)) as an illustrative bound (not a code rule) and check that thin 15 mm caps drop below lambda_b = 3.0.

architecture.subtitle: Continuing Folio A.01's funicular thrust surfaces and A.13's inverted-hanging concrete shells: a structural design study of how hyperbolic paraboloid (hypar) geometry uses straight timber plank rulings to form doubly curved 40 mm concrete umbrellas (12.0 m quadrant semi-span, 4.0 m rise), mapping Pucher's flat-projection membrane shear model (N_xy = 31.35 kN/m, σ_2 = -0.784 MPa) alongside cantilevered free-edge, valley-rib, and thin-shell buckling boundaries.
architecture.governing_law: z = (h / (a b)) x y · N_xy = (q_0 a b) / (2 h) · σ_1 = +N_xy / t · σ_2 = -N_xy / t · M_x = M_y = 0

colophon.identifier: A.14 · Félix Candela Hypar Ruled Shells & Pucher Membrane Shear · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: Doubly-Ruled Hypar Saddle · Pucher Flat-Projection Shear · 45-Degree Principal Arch-Tie Field
colophon.benchmarks: Model values (not measurements): a = b = 12.0 m · h = 4.0 m · t = 40.0 mm · q_0 = 1.741 kN/m² · N_xy = 31.35 kN/m · σ_2 = -0.784 MPa · λ_comp = 20.1 · 80.0% shell-field thickness saving vs 200 mm slab · Q_storm = 8.0 L/s (576 m²)
colophon.bridge: Continues A.01/A.13 · Idealized Pucher membrane shear vs. cantilevered free-edge & rib behavior

steps: Stage 1 (Doubly-Ruled Hypar Geometry & Unbent Timber Formwork): A hyperbolic paraboloid quadrant z(x, y) = (h / (a b)) x y has negative Gaussian curvature everywhere (an anticlastic saddle) yet contains two families of straight generating lines along constant x and constant y. Because every section parallel to the axes is a straight line, builders could assemble formwork from unbent straight timber planks without curved falsework (Cassinello et al. 2010, DOI 10.3989/ic.10.040; Garlock & Billington 2011, DOI 10.2749/101686611x13049248220564).

Stage 2 (Pucher Projected Membrane Equilibrium): Under uniform plan-projected gravity load q_0 = 1.741 kN/m² (40.0 mm concrete at ρ = 2,400 kg/m³ giving 0.941 kN/m² plus 0.80 kN/m² superimposed load), Pucher's 1934 projected equilibrium equation cancels normal membrane terms because ∂²z/∂x² = 0 and ∂²z/∂y² = 0 identically. In this idealized interior membrane model with supported edges, N_x = N_y = M_x = M_y = 0 and uniform shear becomes N_xy = (q_0 a b) / (2 h) = 31.35 kN/m.

Stage 3 (Diagonal Principal Arch-Tie Field & Thickness Ratio): Rotating 45 degrees onto the bisecting diagonals resolves pure shear into equal principal tension σ_1 = +N_xy / t = +0.784 MPa and principal compression σ_2 = -N_xy / t = -0.784 MPa. Against an allowable compressive threshold of 0.45 f_ck = 15.75 MPa (f_ck = 35 MPa), the model compressive ratio is λ_comp = 20.1, while the 40 mm shell field uses 80.0% less concrete volume than a 200 mm solid flat slab (excluding stem and ribs).

Stage 4 (Central Stormwater Funnel & Tier T2 Model Boundary): Grouping four quadrants into a 24.0 m by 24.0 m (576 m²) umbrella slopes rainwater inward toward a central hollow stem, collecting 8.0 L/s (28.8 m³/h) under 50 mm/h design rain. Hypothesis (Tier T2 analytical model): straight-ruled anticlastic curvature carries symmetric gravity load primarily in in-plane shear rather than bending. This flat-projection model is falsified for physical cantilevered umbrellas where slope-angle self-weight growth, free-edge boundary bending, valley-rib concentration, concrete creep, or thin-shell buckling (Ramm & Mehlhorn 1991, DOI 10.1016/0141-0296(91)90050-M; Wang et al. 2020, DOI 10.1016/j.engstruct.2020.111156) govern failure.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE A.14-A · OVER 800 THIN SHELLS IN MEXICO CITY & BEYOND
sidenote_1.body: Cassinello, Schlaich, and Torroja (2010, DOI 10.3989/ic.10.040) document how Spanish-born architect-engineer Félix Candela built more than 800 reinforced-concrete thin shells—chiefly in Mexico—pairing doubly curved strength with low-cost carpentry. Billington and Garlock (2010, DOI 10.1061/(asce)st.1943-541x.0000144) and Garlock and Billington (2011, DOI 10.2749/101686611x13049248220564) examine how Candela united economy, efficiency, and sculptural form.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE A.14-B · STRAIGHT RULINGS VS. CANTILEVER EDGE BENDING
sidenote_2.body: Because z = (h / (a b)) x y has zero second partial derivatives along the x and y axes, Pucher's 1934 projected membrane equation yields constant shear N_xy = q_0 a b / (2 h) when edges carry tangential shear. In physical cantilevered umbrellas (Candela 1960, DOI 10.14359/8026; Wang et al. 2020, DOI 10.1016/j.engstruct.2020.111156; Wang et al. 2022, DOI 10.1016/j.engstruct.2022.114577), free outer edges and central valley intersections alter shear flow and demand nonlinear ultimate-load analysis (Ramm & Mehlhorn 1991, DOI 10.1016/0141-0296(91)90050-M).

skill.description: AI-agnostic architectural and structural engineering skill for Félix Candela's doubly-ruled hyperbolic paraboloid (hypar) concrete shells, Pucher flat-projection membrane shear equilibrium, and idealized cantilever/rib bounds.
rules: Define one quadrant of a hyperbolic paraboloid saddle as z(x, y) = (h / (a * b)) * x * y with twist parameter c = (a * b) / h.
Compute Pucher flat-projection membrane shear resultant as N_xy = (q_0 * a * b) / (2 * h) under uniform projected gravity load q_0, noting omitted slope-angle weight amplification.
Resolve 45-degree principal stresses as sigma_1 = +N_xy / t (tension) and sigma_2 = -N_xy / t (compression) in the idealized interior membrane model.
Evaluate compressive margin lambda_comp = (0.45 * f_ck) / |sigma_2| alongside shell-field thickness savings relative to a 200 mm slab, and flag free-edge bending and buckling limits.

sliders.label: Exponent Axiom Mutation (p = 2 Pythagorean vs p ≥ 3)

steps: Stage 1 (Frey Curve & Semistability): Maps a^p + b^p = c^p to a semistable elliptic curve E/Q with minimal discriminant Δ_E = 2^(-8)(abc)^(2p).
Stage 2 (Ribet Level-Lowering): Establishes that the mod-p Galois representation ρ_{E,p} is modular of level N = 2, creating a high-energy deductive bottleneck.

Stage 3 (Taylor-Wiles R_Q = T_Q Patching): Auxiliary sets of primes Q_N make the comparison of R and T tractable. The folio draws this as a barrier falling from 8.39 to 3.59 in kcal/mol-style units; those two numbers are illustrative model values, not quantities found in the mathematics.
Stage 4 (Cusp Form Contradiction): Forces ρ_{E,p} into weight-2 cusp forms S_2(Γ_0(2)), where dim S_2(Γ_0(2)) = 0 closes the proof.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.01-A · COUNTERFACTUAL P = 2
sidenote_1.body: For exponent 2 the equation has solutions, such as 3² + 4² = 5², so the argument must fail there, and it does: the Frey-curve contradiction is only available for exponents of 3 and above. In the folio's model the flux readout drops to 3.2% at p = 2, an illustrative value. Comparing this with a truncated ion channel is a loose analogy and nothing more.

The folio borrows only the picture of two aids doing together what one cannot. No mathematics passes between number theory and protein folding.

math.title: Riemann Zeta Zero-Density Estimates and Large Sieve Inequalities
math.subtitle: Classical zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function, and what a public Lean 4 repository README states about a recent critical-line result. The comparison with Markov-chain relaxation is this folio's own analogy.

colophon.identifier: M.02 · Analytic Number Theory
colophon.kernels: Zero-density estimates · Large Sieve · Zeta23 (README statement)
colophon.benchmarks: Ingham-Huxley Zero-Density N(σ, T) ≪ T^(c(1-σ)+ε), total exponent 3/5 at σ = 3/4
colophon.bridge: Spectral gap ↔ Markov-chain relaxation (analogy only)

sliders.label: Real Part Threshold σ in Critical Strip (1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1)

steps: Stage 1 (Dirichlet Polynomial Mollification): A mollifier M(s) is a short Dirichlet polynomial chosen so that ζ(s)M(s) stays close to 1 away from zeros; it is a standard tool for studying zeros near the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.
Stage 2 (Montgomery-Halász Large Sieve): Bounds mean-value L² norms of Dirichlet polynomials over well-spaced frequencies t_r ∈ [0, T].
Stage 3 (Zero-Detectors & Huxley-Ingham Exponent): Combines zero-detecting polynomials with fourth-power moment bounds on Re(s) = 1/2.

Stage 4 (The Resulting Bound): Zero-density estimates of the form N(σ, T) ≪ T^(c(1-σ)+ε) limit how many zeros can lie off the critical line. Ingham gives c = 3/(2-σ) and Huxley gives c = 12/5; at σ = 3/4 both give c = 12/5 and the total exponent c(1-σ) = 3/5. Comparing this with a spectral gap is the folio's own analogy.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.02-A · WHAT THE REPOSITORY STATES
sidenote_1.body: The README of anthropics/formal-math lists a Zeta23 project whose statement is that more than two thirds of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line (Alpöge–Furman, arXiv:2608.13637). This site has not built it and does not check the mathematics. The same project contains zeta23/Challenge/XiPrime.lean, whose header describes it as a challenge about the zeros of ξ′ (the derivative of the completed zeta function); this folio does not use it, and its proof status was not checked here.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.02-B · A LOOSE ANALOGY WITH MARKOV CHAINS
sidenote_2.body: For a reversible continuous-time Markov chain, the relaxation time is the reciprocal of the spectral gap, τ = 1/λ_2. The folio places this picture beside zero-density bounds only as an analogy: no mathematics passes between the zeros of zeta and the gating of an ion channel.

math.title: Extremal Cap Sets in F_3^n, Polynomial Method Upper Bounds, and Rank-48 Matrix Tensors
math.subtitle: What two published Google DeepMind systems report about large cap sets in F_3^8 (FunSearch: a set of 512 points) and about multiplying 4×4 complex matrices with 48 scalar multiplications (AlphaEvolve). Any link to biology is an analogy.

colophon.identifier: M.03 · Extremal Combinatorics & Tensors
colophon.kernels: FunSearch Cap Set (512 in F_3^8) · AlphaEvolve 48 products
colophon.benchmarks: Ellenberg-Gijswijt o(2.756^n) · 512^(1/8) = 2.1810 (products)
colophon.bridge: Line-free sets ↔ constrained sequence design (analogy only)

sliders.label: Affine Dimension n in F_3^n (3 ≤ n ≤ 8)
Tensor Border Rank Target (4×4 Matrix Multiplication)

steps: Stage 1 (Affine Line-Free Constraint): A subset S ⊂ F_3^n is a Cap Set if no three distinct vectors x, y, z ∈ S satisfy x + y + z = 0 (mod 3).
Stage 2 (Croot-Lev-Pach & Ellenberg-Gijswijt Polynomial Method): The polynomial method bounds the size of a cap set in F_3^n by o(2.756^n) (Ellenberg-Gijswijt, Corollary 5).
Stage 3 (FunSearch Priority-Function Discovery): Romera-Paredes et al. report an evolutionary search over Python priority functions that found a 512-point cap set in F_3^8.

Stage 4 (AlphaEvolve 48-Product Procedure): The AlphaEvolve white paper reports a procedure for 4×4 complex matrices with 48 scalar multiplications, against the 49 that Strassen's 1969 method gives when applied twice (7² = 49).

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.03-A · NATURE DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06924-6
sidenote_1.body: The Nature paper reports that FunSearch searches for programs that describe how to build a solution rather than for the solution itself, and that such programs tend to be more interpretable than raw solutions. Its Figure 4b shows the priority function that yields a cap set of 512 points in dimension 8.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.03-B · A LOOSE ANALOGY
sidenote_2.body: Choosing a sequence that avoids forbidden patterns can be compared in spirit with building a cap set, which avoids a forbidden pattern of three points. The folio draws that comparison only as an analogy. It names no real design method, and nothing here is medical advice.

Verify bilinear tensor decomposition sum_{r=1}^R (u_r . A)(v_r . B) w_r = A B exactly satisfies all n^6 Brent equations.

math.title: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa (PFR) Entropy Calculus and the 22-Million Equational Magma Graph
math.subtitle: A reading of the entropy proof of the Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture in characteristic 2 (Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao), the public Lean 4 project whose README says it formalizes that proof, and the Equational Theories project's 4,694 magma laws and 22,028,942 ordered pairs. The comparison with genetics is an analogy.

steps: Stage 1 (Small Doubling Hypothesis): A subset A ⊂ F_2^n satisfies |A + A| ≤ K|A|, indicating hidden approximate subgroup structure.
Stage 2 (Ruzsa Entropic Triangle Inequality): Defines entropic distance d(X, Y) = H(X - Y') - (H(X) + H(Y'))/2 and evaluates submodularity bounds.

Stage 3 (Tau-Minimizer): The proof studies a minimizer of an entropic functional τ and uses it to show that d(X, U_H) is small for the uniform distribution U_H on a subgroup H. This page's slider is a simplified picture of that step, not the paper's argument.

Stage 4 (Polynomial Coset Covering): The theorem, as stated in the README of the Lean project, says A is covered by at most 2·K^12 cosets of a subspace H of size at most |A|. Separately, the Equational Theories project concerns 4,694 × 4,693 = 22,028,942 ordered pairs of magma laws.

math.title: Sub-Cubic Fine-Grained Reductions (3SUM → APSP) and Step-Level Process Supervision (PRM800K)
math.subtitle: Ryan Williams's circuit-complexity algorithm for All-Pairs Shortest Paths, a repository README's statement of a polynomial improvement for APSP and 3SUM, and OpenAI's step-level process-supervision paper. Comparisons with proof search or genomics are this folio's own analogies.

colophon.identifier: M.06 · Fine-Grained Complexity & PRM
colophon.kernels: Williams APSP · 3SUM · Step-Level PRM
colophon.bridge: Search pruning ↔ screening many candidates (analogy only)

steps: Stage 1 (Min-Plus Distance Product): Formulates All-Pairs Shortest Paths as (A ⋆ B)_{ij} = min_k (A_{ik} + B_{kj}) over n = 4,096 vertices.

Stage 2 (Razborov-Smolensky Polynomial Batching): Williams uses Razborov-Smolensky polynomials over F_2 to reduce a min-plus product to a relatively small number of rectangular matrix products (SIAM J. Comput. 2018, abstract).

Stage 3 (Step-Level Scoring): A process reward model scores each step of a solution. Lightman et al. report that process supervision significantly outperformed outcome supervision on problems from the MATH dataset (arXiv:2305.20050).

Stage 4 (Illustrative Numbers): The figures on this page are illustrative. A cubic count at n = 4,096 is 4,096³ = 6.87 × 10^10 operations; 14.8 is an assumed divisor that no theorem implies. A 20-step chain whose validity is the product of per-step probabilities gives 0.9566^20 ≈ 41.2% and 0.99723^20 ≈ 94.6%. None of these is a measured result.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.06-A · SIAM DOI 10.1137/15M1024524
sidenote_1.body: Williams's abstract describes a randomized algorithm that computes the min-plus product, and so APSP, in time n^3/2^(Ω(log n)^(1/2)) on the real RAM, where earlier algorithms took O(n^3/log^c n) for c ≤ 2. It uses Razborov-Smolensky polynomials to reduce the product to rectangular matrix products over F_2; a deterministic version runs in n^3/2^(log^δ n) for some δ > 0.

sidenote_2.body: The folio compares pruning a search early with screening many candidate sequences. This is an analogy only. Nothing here was run on a genome, and nothing here is a method for designing guide RNAs.

sidenote_1.body: By Pontryagin's adjoint equation dλ_E/ds = −∂H/∂E_batt, whenever battery energy E_batt(s) stays inside [E_min, E_max] and losses omit state of charge, ∂H/∂E_batt = 0, so one constant shadow price λ_E* governs the lap.

rules: Formulate the minimum-Hamiltonian H = (1/v) + lambda_v * a_net(v, P_k, delta_wing) / v - lambda_E * P_batt(P_k) / v along arc-length s, with P_batt = P_k / eta_k for motoring (P_k >= 0) and eta_regen * P_k under braking.

Evaluate the motoring optimality condition dH/dP_k = lambda_v / (m * v^2) - lambda_E * (dP_batt/dP_k) / v = 0 (lambda_v, lambda_E < 0 under min_u H): affine losses (dP_batt/dP_k = 1/eta_k) switch at lambda_v / (m * v) = lambda_E / eta_k, whereas strictly convex losses P_batt(P_k) initiate smooth tapering below P_k,max where lambda_v / (m * v) = lambda_E * dP_batt/dP_k(P_k,max).
Evaluate spectral neural operator layer u_{l+1}(x) = sigma(W * u_l(x) + F^{-1}(R_phi * F(u_l))(x)) truncated at k_max Fourier modes.

math.title: Riemannian Differential Geometry of Color Perception: Helmholtz–Schrödinger Geodesics, MacAdam Metric Tensors & Grassmann Spectral Hilbert Projections
math.subtitle: How the linearity of color matching that Hermann Grassmann described, read in modern terms as a projection Π: L²([380,780] nm) → ℝ³, creates metamers, and how a Riemannian line element ds² = g_ij dx^i dx^j of the kind Erwin Schrödinger proposed in 1920 defines curved paths between hues. The numbers shown are model values.

steps: Stage 1 (Grassmann Hilbert Space Projection Π: L² → ℝ³₊): Continuous electromagnetic spectra I(λ) project onto 3 cone coordinates X_k = ∫ S(λ, T_illum) R(λ) c̄_k(λ) dλ.

Stage 2 (Cohen's Fundamental Metamer Decomposition): Because dim ker(Π) = ∞, any spectrum decomposes into R(λ) = R*(λ) + B(λ), where metameric black B(λ) vanishes under D65 (6500 K) but emerges at sunset (3000 K).

Stage 3 (Helmholtz-Type Line Element g_ij, the folio's model): Discrimination ellipses such as those MacAdam measured in 1942 show that equal perceptual steps are not equal Euclidean steps. The folio models this with a Helmholtz-type line element ds² = ∑ a_k (dx^k / x^k)².

Stage 4 (Geodesic Hue Interpolation, model): Solvingẍ^k + Γ^k_ij ẋ^i ẋ^j = 0 for that model metric between a cobalt blue and a magenta (rosa mexicano) gives a curved path. The +9.4° hue difference from a flat RGB chord is an illustrative model value, not a measured Abney-effect correction.

math.subtitle: Synthesizing Folios M.04, M.07, and M.08: how Jean-David Benamou & Yann Brenier recast quadratic Wasserstein-2 optimal transport as a fluid-mechanics problem of least kinetic energy, with a pressureless flow guided by a Hamilton–Jacobi potential. The numbers shown are illustrative model values.

colophon.identifier: M.09 · Benamou–Brenier Wasserstein-2 Optimal Transport
colophon.kernels: Benamou–Brenier Fluid Geodesic · Brenier Convex Potential ∇Φ · Sinkhorn KL
colophon.benchmarks: Illustrative model values: W_2²(μ_0, μ_1) = 4.82 · t = 0.50 · ε = 0.05 (18 Sinkhorn steps)
colophon.bridge: Synthesizes M.04/M.07/M.08 · Waddington-OT trajectory inference (Schiebinger et al. 2019) as a method reference

steps: Stage 1 (Monge–Kantorovich Convex Duality): Relaxes Monge's transport map T_# μ_0 = μ_1 into Kantorovich's linear program over couplings π ∈ Π(μ_0, μ_1).
Stage 2 (Brenier Polar Factorization Theorem): Shows the unique L²-optimal transport map is the gradient of a convex potential T(x) = ∇Φ(x) = x + ∇ψ_0(x).
Stage 3 (Benamou–Brenier Dynamic Fluid Geodesic, DOI 10.1007/s002110050002): Evolves density ρ_t along constant-velocity geodesics ∂_t ρ + ∇·(ρ∇ψ) = 0 with HJB optimality ∂_t ψ + ½|∇ψ|² = 0.

Stage 4 (Cuturi Sinkhorn Scaling, Continuing M.04/M.07): The entropic penalty ε KL(π || μ_0⊗μ_1) turns the problem into alternating matrix scalings. The 18-step count shown is an illustrative value; the real count depends on ε and the stopping tolerance.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.09-A · UNITING M.04 ENTROPY, M.07 HJB & M.08 RIEMANNIAN METRICS
sidenote_1.body: In Felix Otto's formal Riemannian calculus on probability space P_2(R^d), Benamou–Brenier paths are geodesics. As ε -> 0, entropic transport plans approach the unregularized optimal plan, whose Brenier map solves the Monge–Ampère equation det(D²Φ) = f / (g ∘ ∇Φ).

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.09-B · WADDINGTON-OT AND A POSSIBLE AIRWAY QUESTION
sidenote_2.body: Because scRNA-seq destroys cells at each measurement timepoint t_k, Schiebinger et al. (2019, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2019.01.006) used optimal transport to infer developmental trajectories during reprogramming. The same method could in principle be asked how airway basal cells give rise to ionocytes, a CFTR-rich cell type described in 2018 (Montoro et al., DOI 10.1038/s41586-018-0393-7; Plasschaert et al., DOI 10.1038/s41586-018-0394-6). This folio has not done that analysis.

colophon.kernels: Vietoris–Rips Filtration · Z_2 Boundary Reduction ∂_k · Bottleneck Stability

steps: Stage 1 (Vietoris–Rips Simplicial Filtration K_ε, Continuing M.05): Grows balls of radius ε around 3D pore/mucin nodes, adding edges, triangles, and tetrahedra as pairwise distances cross 2ε.
Stage 2 (Chain Complex & Z_2 Boundary Reduction ∂_{k−1} ∘ ∂_k = 0, DOI 10.1007/s00454-002-2885-2): Reduces boundary matrices to pair each k-cycle birth b_i with its bounding (k+1)-simplex death d_i.

Stage 3 (Cohen-Steiner Bottleneck Stability): By the stability theorem of Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner & Harer, a perturbation moves persistence points by at most d_B ≤ ||f − g||_∞, so short bars near the diagonal can be read as noise and long bars as structure. σ_noise = 0.08 is the model setting.

Stage 4 (Pore-Throat Reading, Completing E.01 & P.03): In the synthetic model the longest H_1 interval is [38 nm, 116 nm]. Robins et al. (2016) relate persistence features of this kind to percolating length scales in micro-CT images of porous materials. Whether a given particle passes through a real mesh also depends on chemistry and binding, which topology alone does not settle.

sidenote_1.body: Folio E.01 introduced percolation (the square-lattice site threshold p_c ≈ 0.5927) and Helmholtz–Hodge decomposition; Folio M.10 adds persistent homology, a way to track connected pieces and loops in 3D point clouds across scales.

The Bottleneck Stability Theorem bounds how far noise can move persistence points, which is why persistence is attractive for noisy images; how well it sizes pores in a particular biological sample would have to be tested.

math.title: The 3D Kakeya Preprint of Wang and Zahl and the Guth–Maynard Zero-Density Estimate
math.subtitle: Continuing Folios M.02 and P.08: Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl's preprint (arXiv:2502.17655), which states a proof that every Kakeya set in ℝ³ has Hausdorff dimension 3, and Larry Guth and James Maynard (Annals of Mathematics, 2026; arXiv:2405.20552) improving the zero-density exponent to 30/13, past the long-standing bound at σ = 3/4 that goes back to Ingham in 1940. The two results are separate; the links drawn between them here are analogies.

colophon.identifier: M.11 · 3D Kakeya Conjecture (arXiv:2502.17655) & Guth–Maynard 30/13 (arXiv:2405.20552)
colophon.kernels: Wang–Zahl volume estimates for unions of tubes · Guth–Maynard large values of Dirichlet polynomials
colophon.benchmarks: dim_H(K_3D) = 3 (Wang–Zahl preprint) · zero-density exponent 30/13 ≈ 2.3077 < 12/5 = 2.400 · primes in short intervals of length x^(17/30+o(1))
colophon.bridge: Continues M.02/P.08 · Turning a needle in 3D space ↔ wave packets (an analogy)

steps: Stage 1 (Besicovitch's 1919 Needle Paradox & The 3D Kakeya Conjecture): A unit needle can be rotated 360° inside a set of arbitrarily tiny volume (measure zero), yet the Kakeya Conjecture asserts its fractal Hausdorff dimension in ℝ³ must still be the full 3.000.

Stage 2 (Wang–Zahl 2025, arXiv:2502.17655): In a preprint, Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl study sets of δ-tubes in ℝ³ in which not too many tubes lie inside a common convex set, and state a proof that the union of such tubes has almost maximal volume, from which they deduce that every Kakeya set in ℝ³ has Minkowski and Hausdorff dimension 3.

Stage 3 (Guth–Maynard, arXiv:2405.20552; Annals 2026): New bounds on how often Dirichlet polynomials take large values give the zero-density estimate N(σ, T) ≤ T^(30(1−σ)/13+o(1)), improving on the uniform exponent 12/5 = 2.40 of Huxley (DOI 10.1007/BF01418933) and on the bound at σ = 3/4 going back to Ingham (1940).

Stage 4 (Consequence and formal context): Guth and Maynard also deduce asymptotics for primes in short intervals of length x^(17/30+o(1)). Neither result is listed in the README of anthropics/formal-math read on 2026-11-14; that README lists Lean 4 projects on other theorems (see Act IV).

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.11-A · CROSS-FIELD ANALOGY · TURNING A NEEDLE IN 3D
sidenote_1.body: How much room do you need to point a needle in every 3D direction? Very little volume, but a preprint by Wang and Zahl states a proof that the set must still have dimension 3. Harmonic analysts care because wave packets behave like thin tubes, and Kakeya-type estimates are linked to restriction problems in Fourier analysis. Claims that this result governs MRI scanners have no source and are not made here.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.11-B · WHAT THE FORMAL-MATH README LISTS
sidenote_2.body: The README of https://github.com/anthropics/formal-math, read on 2026-11-14, describes its zeta23 project as a machine-checked Lean 4 formalisation of the Alpöge–Furman result that more than two thirds of zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line (arXiv:2608.13637); the project's file tree read the same day also holds Challenge/XiPrime.lean, on the zeros of ξ′. That README does not list Guth–Maynard or Wang–Zahl. https://github.com/openai/math is a separate repository whose contents were not reviewed for this folio. This site has not built either.

colophon.bridge: Synthesizes M.01/M.03/M.06 · Egg carton in fog (analogy) ↔ post-quantum key exchange

steps: Stage 1 (Shor's Quantum Period-Finding): Shor's 1994 algorithm would let a large fault-tolerant quantum computer (Folio P.11) find the period r of a^x mod N in time polynomial in log N, which would break RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography. No quantum computer able to do this for cryptographic key sizes has been reported.

Stage 2 (Module Learning With Errors, NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM): The public key b = A s + e (mod q = 3329) over the ring R_q = ℤ_q[X]/(X²⁵⁶ + 1) hides the secret s behind small centered binomial noise e. Its security rests on the presumed hardness of module lattice problems; Regev (2009) showed that plain LWE is at least as hard, under a quantum reduction, as certain worst-case lattice problems.

Stage 3 (What anthropics/formal-math says it contains): The README of anthropics/formal-math, read on 2026-11-14, lists three Lean 4 projects: zeta23 (Alpöge–Furman on zeta zeros), 3sum-apsp (Alman–Vassilevska Williams on 3SUM and APSP) and eth, described there as an algorithm for counting k-CNF solutions that refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis. This site has not built or checked any of them. Earlier editions named files EightSquare.lean, ThreeSUM_APSP.lean and ETHIsFalse.lean; no files of those names appear in the repository's file tree read on 2026-11-14.

Stage 4 (Implementation): open-quantum-safe/liboqs is an open-source library of post-quantum algorithms. Formal proofs about mathematics do not by themselves make an implementation bug-free; verifying cryptographic code is a separate task.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.12-A · CROSS-FIELD ANALOGY · A 768-DIMENSIONAL EGG CARTON IN THICK FOG
sidenote_1.body: Why is ML-KEM thought to resist quantum computers? Picture an egg carton stretched across 768 dimensions: the secret is a grid point, the public key drops you near it in fog (+e), and finding the nearest valley without the secret is believed to be hard for classical and quantum computers alike. That belief rests on decades of cryptanalysis, not on a proof.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.12-B · WHAT THE ANTHROPICS/FORMAL-MATH README LISTS
sidenote_2.body: The README of https://github.com/anthropics/formal-math, read on 2026-11-14, lists three projects: zeta23, 3sum-apsp and eth. It states a deterministic algorithm that counts satisfying assignments of every k-CNF in 2^O(min{k²n log log n/√log n, km/√log m}) steps, which it says refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis. That is an extraordinary claim; this site reports it as the repository's statement and has not checked it. The README of https://github.com/anthropics/fermats-last-theorem, read the same day, describes it as a separate Lean 4 repository holding a machine-checked proof of Fermat's Last Theorem.

math.title: Shannon Zero-Error Graph Capacity, Lovász Theta Sandwich & the Open Seven-Cycle Gap
math.subtitle: How Claude Shannon turned error-free messaging into packing squares on cyclic graphs, how László Lovász settled the five-cycle with a three-dimensional umbrella, why Willem Haemers separated geometric cones from capacity on twenty-seven lines, and why the seven-cycle limit stays open.
math.governing_law: α(G) ≤ Θ(G) ≤ ϑ(G) ≤ α*(G) ≤ χ̄(G) · ϑ(C_n) = n cos(π/n) / [1 + cos(π/n)]

colophon.identifier: M.13 · Zero-Error Capacity & Lovász Theta Sandwich · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: Shannon Strong Product G^k · Lovász Umbrella ϑ(G) · Haemers Minrank(S_bar) = 7
colophon.bridge: Extends M.03/M.06 · Information-theoretic packing and spectral duality

steps: Stage 1 (Confusability Graphs and Strong Products, Shannon 1956): Claude Shannon (DOI 10.1109/TIT.1956.1056798) modeled a noisy discrete channel as a graph G whose vertices are input letters and whose edges connect pairs that can produce the same output. Zero-error words of length k form an independent set in the k-fold strong product G^k, yielding Θ(G) = sup_k α(G^k)^(1/k). For C_5, α(C_5) = 2, whereas the five pairs (i, 2i mod 5) form an independent set in C_5^2, giving Θ(C_5) ≥ √5.

Stage 2 (Lovász Orthonormal Umbrellas and Sandwich Inequality, 1979): László Lovász (DOI 10.1109/TIT.1979.1055985) defined ϑ(G) by placing unit vectors u_i in Euclidean space so non-adjacent vertices are orthogonal, minimizing max_i 1/(c · u_i)^2 over unit handles c. Because ϑ is multiplicative under strong products, α(G) ≤ Θ(G) ≤ ϑ(G) ≤ α*(G) ≤ χ̄(G). On odd cycles, ϑ(C_n) = n cos(π/n) / [1 + cos(π/n)], pinning Θ(C_5) = √5 ≈ 2.236068 via the 3D umbrella cos²φ = 1/√5.

Stage 3 (Haemers Minrank Separation on the Schläfli Complement, 1979): Willem Haemers (DOI 10.1109/TIT.1979.1056027) bounded Θ(G) above by the minimum rank of any matrix fitting G over a field. On the 27-line cubic-surface intersection graph S_bar = SRG(27, 10, 1, 5), spectrum {10^1, 1^20, (-5)^6} gives ϑ(S_bar) = 9, whereas A(S_bar) − I fits S_bar with exact rational rank 7. Thus Θ(S_bar) ≤ 7 < 9, and the diagonal in S ⊠ S_bar shows Θ(S ⊠ S_bar) ≥ 27 > 3 × 7 ≥ Θ(S) Θ(S_bar).

Stage 4 (Open Hypothesis on C_7, Tier T0–T1 Bounds, and Falsification Condition): For the seven-cycle C_7, Polak & Schrijver (2019, DOI 10.1016/j.ipl.2018.11.006) found 367 independent vertices in C_7^5, establishing Tier T0/T1 bounds 367^(1/5) ≈ 3.257866 ≤ Θ(C_7) ≤ ϑ(C_7) ≈ 3.317667. Whether Θ(C_7) equals ϑ(C_7) or stays strictly below it remains OPEN. Any strict algebraic upper bound below 3.317667 refutes equality Θ(C_7) = ϑ(C_7), while any block code with α(C_7^k)^(1/k) > 3.257866 tightens the lower floor.

spec_plate.title: Odd-Cycle Zero-Error Packing Envelope, Lovász Orthonormal Umbrella & Haemers Rank Bound
spec_plate.body: Exact discrete mathematics verification over odd cycles C_5 through C_13, strong products C_5^2 and C_7^2, and the 27-vertex Schläfli complement SRG(27, 10, 1, 5). Lower bounds for C_7^5 (367 codewords) are cited from Polak & Schrijver (2019); all C_5^2, C_7^2, Gram PSD eigenvalues, and exact rational Gaussian-elimination rank-7 checks are recomputed from scratch by verify_m13_shannon_capacity.py.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.13-A · POLYNOMIAL-TIME SDP VS. NP-HARD ALPHA
sidenote_1.body: Grötschel, Lovász & Schrijver (1981, DOI 10.1007/BF02579273) showed via the ellipsoid method that ϑ(G) can be approximated to arbitrary rational precision in polynomial time, even though both α(G) and χ̄(G) are NP-hard. Whenever α(G) = χ̄(G) (perfect graphs), the sandwich collapses to equality and yields both quantities in polynomial time.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.13-B · NON-ADDITIVITY UNDER DISJOINT UNION (ALON 1998)
sidenote_2.body: Shannon asked in 1956 whether the capacity of a disjoint union equals the sum Θ(G ⊔ H) = Θ(G) + Θ(H). Noga Alon (1998, DOI 10.1007/PL00009824) constructed graphs G and H for which Θ(G) and Θ(H) are bounded while Θ(G ⊔ H) grows far larger, demonstrating that block-coding across two separate channels can mix codewords more efficiently than either channel separately.

rules: Model zero-error k-symbol block codes as independent sets in the strong product G^{ oxtimes k}, never the Cartesian box product, so symbol confusability across simultaneous coordinates is captured.
Enforce the Lovasz sandwich alpha(G) <= Theta(G) <= vartheta(G) <= alpha*(G) <= chi_bar(G) and compute odd-cycle theta values via n * cos(pi/n) / (1 + cos(pi/n)).
Never treat vartheta(G) as equal to Theta(G) in general: check algebraic minrank bounds such as Haemers rank(A(S_bar) - I) = 7 < 9 = vartheta(S_bar) on the 27-vertex Schlafli complement.
Keep Theta(C_7) explicitly labeled OPEN between the verified lower floor 367^(1/5) (~3.257866) and the Lovasz upper bound vartheta(C_7) (~3.317667).

math.title: Sphere Packing in Dimensions 3, 4, 8 & 24: Cohn–Elkies Bounds, Modular Functions & Open Gaps
math.subtitle: Synthesizing Folio M.09 energy transport and Folio M.12 lattice geometry: how Henry Cohn and Noam Elkies turned sphere packing into Fourier linear programming, how Maryna Viazovska and collaborators closed dimensions 8 and 24 via modular forms, and why dimension 4 and asymptotic space remain open.

colophon.identifier: M.14 · Sphere Packing, Cohn–Elkies LP & Open Gaps · REV 1.0
colophon.kernels: Laguerre–Gaussian Fourier Eigenbasis · Descartes Shift Check · Golay G_24 Leech Enumeration
colophon.bridge: Synthesizes M.09/M.12

steps: Stage 1 (Lattice Geometry & Kissing Numbers from d = 2 to d = 24): Packing equal spheres in Euclidean space asks what fraction of volume non-overlapping balls can fill. In dimension 2 the hexagonal lattice A_2 fills π/√12 ≈ 0.906900 with 6 neighbors; in dimension 3, Hales et al. (2017, DOI 10.1017/fmp.2017.1) completed the formal Flyspeck check of the Kepler conjecture at π/(3√2) ≈ 0.740480 with 12 neighbors. In dimension 4, the checkerboard lattice D_4 has density π²/16 ≈ 0.616850 and Musin (2008, DOI 10.4007/annals.2008.168.1) settled the kissing number at τ_4 = 24, yet packing optimality in dimension 4 remains open.

Stage 2 (Cohn–Elkies Fourier Linear Programming Duality): Cohn and Elkies (2003, DOI 10.4007/annals.2003.157.689) showed that any radial Schwartz function f with f(0) = f̂(0) > 0, dual non-negativity f̂(t) ≥ 0 everywhere, and primal non-positivity f(x) ≤ 0 for |x| ≥ r_cut yields an upper bound Δ_d ≤ Vol(B_d(r_cut/2)) · f(0)/f̂(0) via the Poisson summation formula. Writing f in the Fourier eigenbasis ψ_k(x) = L_k^(d/2−1)(2π|x|²) exp(−π|x|²) with exact eigenvalue (−1)^k lets our offline verifier construct rational Laguerre–Gaussian test polynomials whose shifted polynomial P(u_cut + w) has every coefficient ≤ 0.

Stage 3 (Viazovska’s Modular Magic Functions in d = 8 and d = 24): In 2017, Viazovska (DOI 10.4007/annals.2017.185.3.7) constructed an infinite modular-form eigenfunction matching the E_8 root lattice (τ_8 = 240, Δ_8 = π⁴/384 ≈ 0.253670) with double roots at every non-minimal shell √(2k). Days later, Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko, and Viazovska (DOI 10.4007/annals.2017.185.3.8) extended the modular construction to the 24-dimensional Leech lattice Λ_24 (Δ_24 = π¹²/12! ≈ 0.001930, τ_24 = 196,560 minimal vectors built from the 759 octads of the extended binary Golay code G_24), and later established universal optimality across radial potentials (2022, DOI 10.4007/annals.2022.196.3.3).

Stage 4 (Open Hypothesis, Tier T0–T2, and Falsification Condition): Hypothesis (Tier T0–T2): finite-degree Laguerre–Gaussian test functions shrink the Cohn–Elkies upper bound monotonically from degree 3 to degree 5 (0.346486 → 0.303541 in d = 8; 0.087466 → 0.008955 in d = 24; 0.700415 → 0.672477 in d = 4), yet leave a roughly 9.0% gap above D_4 in dimension 4 while recent preprints push high-dimensional lower bounds upward via graph independence (arXiv:2312.10026) and stochastic ellipsoids (arXiv:2504.05042). This polynomial gap hypothesis would be falsified if an explicit non-lattice packing in dimension 4 exceeded π²/16 or if an admissible degree-5 Laguerre polynomial dropped below 0.616850; our deterministic checks inspect finite dimensions only and do not re-derive the asymptotic preprint bounds.

spec_plate.title: Exact Rational Laguerre–Gaussian Bounds, E_8 & Golay G_24 Leech Lattice Enumeration
spec_plate.body: Offline verification specification: under the Fourier transform f̂(t) = ∫ f(x) exp(−2πi x·t) dx, radial eigenfunctions L_k^(d/2−1)(2π|x|²) exp(−π|x|²) carry eigenvalue (−1)^k. Setting P̂(u) = (u + α)∏(u − s_j)² in exact rational arithmetic guarantees f̂(t) ≥ 0, while checking that every coefficient of shifted P(u_cut + w) is ≤ 0 establishes f(x) ≤ 0 for |x| ≥ r_cut. Finite-degree bounds (M = 3, 5) strictly bound lattice densities from above without reaching the infinite modular-form optimum.

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.14-A · FOURIER EIGENVALUE PARITY & WHY ODD POLYNOMIAL DEGREE MATTERS
sidenote_1.body: In the Laguerre–Gaussian radial basis ψ_k(x) = L_k^(d/2−1)(2π|x|²) exp(−π|x|²), even-index modes have Fourier eigenvalue +1 while odd-index modes have eigenvalue −1. Choosing an odd-degree dual polynomial P̂(u) = (u + α)∏(u − s_j)² keeps P̂(u) ≥ 0 everywhere on [0, ∞) via positive leading term +u^(2m+1), while the (−1)^(2m+1) flip drives the primal polynomial P(u) → −∞ as u → ∞ so f(x) ≤ 0 holds past r_cut.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.14-B · FROM THE 24-BIT GOLAY CODE G_24 TO 196,560 LEECH SPHERES
sidenote_2.body: The Leech lattice Λ_24 achieves density π¹²/12! ≈ 0.001930 without a single root vector of squared norm 2. Its 196,560 minimal vectors of squared norm 4 (unscaled norm² = 32 in (1/√8) ℤ²⁴ coordinates) decompose cleanly via the 4,096 codewords of the extended binary Golay code G_24: 1,104 Type A vectors of shape ((±4)², 0²²), 97,152 octad vectors from 759 weight-8 codewords (759 × 2⁷), and 98,304 parity vectors of shape ((±1)²³, ∓3) (24 × 2¹²), verified by direct codeword enumeration in verify_m14_sphere_packing.py.

steps: Stage 1 (Small Settled Thresholds and Goodman Multiplicity, 1930–1959): Frank Ramsey (1930, DOI 10.1112/plms/s2-30.1.264) showed that every two-coloring of a large enough complete graph contains a monochromatic k-clique. On five vertices, a red pentagon C_5 and its blue pentagram complement avoid monochromatic triangles, whereas on K_6 Goodman’s degree identity (1959, DOI 10.1080/00029890.1959.11989408) gives T_mono = 20 − (1/2)∑ d_r(v)(5 − d_r(v)) ≥ 2 across all 32,768 colorings (attained 1,760 times), pinning R(3, 3) = 6. On eight vertices, the circulant step set {1, 4, 7} avoids red K_3 and blue K_4, while forced 3-regularity on K_9 gives odd degree sum 9 × 3 = 27, pinning R(3, 4) = 9.

Stage 2 (Quadratic Residues on F_17 and the Open Five-Clique Window, 1955–2026): Greenwood and Gleason (1955, DOI 10.4153/CJM-1955-001-4) colored K_17 by connecting u and v in red whenever (v − u) mod 17 lies in the quadratic residue set {1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 13, 15, 16}. Multiplication by non-residue 3 mod 17 swaps red and blue edges, yielding strongly regular Paley graph P(17) = SRG(17, 8, 3, 4) with zero monochromatic K_4 across all 2,380 four-subsets; combining with R(4, 4) ≤ R(3, 4) + R(4, 3) = 18 settles R(4, 4) = 18. By contrast, R(5, 5) stays open between 43 (Exoo 1989, DOI 10.1002/jgt.3190130113) and 46 (Angeltveit & McKay 2026, DOI 10.1002/jgt.70029).

Stage 3 (Erdős First-Moment Floor, Convexity at p = 1/2, and Spencer’s Local Lemma, 1947–1975): Paul Erdős (1947, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9904-1947-08785-1) counted colorings at p = 1/2; this folio extends the same count to a general red probability p, giving expected monochromatic k-cliques E[X_k(n, p)] = C(n, k)[p^C(k,2) + (1 − p)^C(k,2)]. Whenever E[X_k(n, p)] < 1, at least one coloring avoids monochromatic K_k, so R(k, k) ≥ n_1(k, p) + 1. Convexity of p^m + (1 − p)^m minimizes E[X_k] at p = 0.50, yielding asymptotic base √2 ≈ 1.414214; Joel Spencer (1975, DOI 10.1016/0097-3165(75)90071-0) doubled the prefactor to (1 + o(1)) (√2/e) k 2^(k/2) via the Lovász Local Lemma.

Stage 4 (Asymmetric Book Algorithm, Tier T0–T1 Hypothesis, and Falsification Conditions, 1988–2026): Thomason (1988, DOI 10.1002/jgt.3190120406), Conlon (2009, DOI 10.4007/annals.2009.170.941), and Sah (2023, DOI 10.1215/00127094-2022-0048) shaved sub-exponential factors off Erdős–Szekeres C(2k − 2, k − 1) < 4^k. Campos, Griffiths, Morris, and Sahasrabudhe (2026, DOI 10.4007/annals.2026.203.3.4) achieved an exponential reduction R(k, k) ≤ (4 − ε)^k for a constant ε > 0 via an asymmetric book algorithm. Hypothesis (Tier T0–T1): skewing p off 0.50 drops n_1(k, p) for every k ≥ 5 (from 100 at p = 0.50 to 71 at p = 0.45 and 17 at p = 0.20 when k = 10), yet finite algebraic colorings beat n_1 + 1 at k = 3, 4, 5 while leaving both R(5, 5) ∈ [43, 46] and whether lim R(k, k)^(1/k) exists inside [√2, 4 − ε] open. Any 43-vertex (K_5, K_5)-free coloring refutes R(5, 5) = 43; any family exceeding base √2 narrows the asymptotic gap from below.

spec_plate.division: EXTREMAL & PROBABILISTIC COMBINATORICS / RAMSEY MULTIPLICITY & DENSITY
spec_plate.title: Exhaustive K_6 Goodman Check, Paley P(17) over F_17 & Rational First-Moment Thresholds
spec_plate.body: Scope boundary: verify_m15_ramsey_bounds.py recomputes offline from scratch all 32,768 two-colorings of K_6 (minimum 2 monochromatic triangles across 1,760 colorings), the Z_8 circulant {1, 4, 7} witness for R(3, 4) > 8, all 2,380 four-subsets of Paley P(17) for R(4, 4) > 17 (the matching upper bounds are the classical degree arguments, restated and not machine-checked), and rational Fraction union bounds across k ∈ [3..10] and p ∈ [0.20..0.80]. The computer-assisted bounds R(5, 5) ≥ 43 (Exoo 1989), R(5, 5) ≤ 46 (Angeltveit & McKay 2026), and R(k, k) ≤ (4 − ε)^k (Campos et al. 2026) are reported from those published papers and are not re-derived by this script.
spec_plate.meta: Primary anchors: Ramsey 1930 (DOI 10.1112/plms/s2-30.1.264) · Erdős 1947 (DOI 10.1090/S0002-9904-1947-08785-1) · Greenwood & Gleason 1955 (DOI 10.4153/CJM-1955-001-4) · Campos, Griffiths, Morris & Sahasrabudhe 2026 (DOI 10.4007/annals.2026.203.3.4) · Angeltveit & McKay 2026 (DOI 10.1002/jgt.70029)

sidenote_1.kicker: SIDENOTE M.15-A · WHY INTEGER PLATEAUS APPEAR AT k = 3 AND k = 4
sidenote_1.body: Although the continuous expectation E[X_k(n, p)] = C(n, k)[p^m + (1 − p)^m] attains a strict minimum at p = 0.50 for every k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k, its integer cutoff n_1(k, p) = max{n : E[X_k(n, p)] < 1} rounds down to whole vertices. At k = 3, E[X_3(4, 0.50)] = 4 × (1/8 + 1/8) = 1, so strict inequality < 1 holds only up to n_1 = 3 across the entire slider interval [0.20, 0.80]; at k = 4, n_1 = 6 stays flat across [0.40, 0.60]. From k = 5 through k = 10, the 0.05 step grid resolves a single peak at p = 0.50.

sidenote_2.kicker: SIDENOTE M.15-B · PALEY QUADRATIC RESIDUES STOP AT FOUR-CLIQUES
sidenote_2.body: Paley graphs P(q) on prime powers q ≡ 1 (mod 4) look statistically random in edge density and eigenvalue spread, and P(17) reaches the sharp threshold 17 = R(4, 4) − 1. Yet Paley constructions do not settle R(5, 5): on prime q = 37, P(37) avoids monochromatic 5-cliques yet falls below Exoo’s 42-vertex coloring (1989, DOI 10.1002/jgt.3190130113), while on prime q = 41, P(41) already contains monochromatic 5-cliques, illustrating how subtle local correlations separate explicit algebraic graphs from uniform random colorings.

skill.name: diagonal-ramsey-paley-book-bounds
skill.description: AI-agnostic extremal and probabilistic combinatorics skill for diagonal Ramsey numbers R(k, k), Goodman triangle multiplicity, Paley P(17), rational Erdos first-moment floors, and asymmetric book bounds.
rules: Require strict inequality E[X_k(n, p)] = C(n, k) * (p^C(k,2) + (1 - p)^C(k,2)) < 1 in rational arithmetic when computing the first-moment witness n_1(k, p), since E = 1 (as at k = 3, n = 4, p = 0.50) permits constant-1 random variables with zero clique-free colorings.
Distinguish continuous expectation minimization at p = 0.50 from integer quantization plateaus of n_1(k, p) at k = 3 (n_1 = 3 across [0.20, 0.80]) and k = 4 (n_1 = 6 across [0.40, 0.60]).

Verify R(3, 3) = 6, R(3, 4) = 9, and R(4, 4) = 18 via explicit witnesses (C_5, Z_8 circulant {1, 4, 7}, and self-complementary Paley P(17) over F_17) paired with Goodman multiplicity and degree-sum parity.

Keep R(5, 5) explicitly labeled OPEN inside [43, 46] (Exoo 1989; Angeltveit & McKay 2026) and state the asymptotic root bracket as lim inf >= sqrt(2) and lim sup <= 4 - epsilon (Campos et al. 2026) without assuming the limit exists or inventing a numerical value for epsilon.
